info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Console API
info.description: The `/admin` surface the back-office console is built on. Generated from the handlers; see ADR-0019. Requests, parameters and outcomes are documented; success bodies are described in prose rather than as schemas (the module docstring explains why). Every failure carries the AIP-193 `ErrorResponse` envelope.

post.summary: A super-admin issues an activation code bound to a device slot.

requestBody.description: The device slot: `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, the device registered under `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`

201.description: Issued. The body carries `activation_code`, `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`, for the setup sheet. It is returned exactly once, since only its hash is stored, and it is spent the first time a box exchanges it for a credential (ADR-0050)

400.description: tenant_id, store_id or device_id is not a ULID

503.description: The activation store or the entropy source is unavailable

post.summary: A super-admin cancels a device slot's still-issued codes.

requestBody.description: The device slot: `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, the device registered under `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`

200.description: Every code issued for the slot and not yet spent is cancelled, as for a setup sheet that went astray. The body carries `revoked`, how many were

400.description: tenant_id, store_id or device_id is not a ULID

get.summary:
Lists the console admins — identity and role only, never a credential. Needs
`console.admins.invite` (owner or admin may view the roster).

200.description: Every console administrator, as an array: `id`, `email`, `name`, `role` and `status`. Never a password hash or a TOTP secret

patch.summary:
Changes an admin's role. Needs `console.admins.manage` (owner). Refuses demoting the last active
owner. `404` if there is no admin with that id.

requestBody.description: `role`: `owner`, `admin`, `ops` or `viewer`

204.description: The role is changed, and audited

400.description: role is not one of the four

404.description: There is no administrator with that id

409.description: The change would demote the last active owner

patch.summary:
Suspends or reactivates an admin. Needs `console.admins.manage` (owner). Refuses suspending the
last active owner. `404` if there is no admin with that id.

requestBody.description: `status`: `active` or `suspended`

204.description: The status is changed, and audited

400.description: status is not `active` or `suspended`

404.description: There is no administrator with that id

409.description: The change would suspend the last active owner

get.summary:
A super-admin (any console role) lists the fleet's alerts: the active set by default, or recent
history (active and resolved, newest-seen first, capped) with `?recent=true`.

parameters.name: recent
parameters.description: `true` for recent history, active and resolved, newest-seen first; absent or `false` for the active alerts only

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: With `recent`, the most alerts to return (default 200)

200.description: The alerts, fleet-wide, as an array: each with `id`, `tenant_id` (absent for a server-wide condition), `kind`, `dedup_key`, `severity` (`info`, `warning` or `critical`), `summary`, `detail`, and the Unix-millisecond instants it was first and last seen, acknowledged and resolved

post.summary: A super-admin holding `console.alerts.manage` acknowledges an alert (idempotent).

204.description: Acknowledged, and audited. Idempotent

post.summary:
A super-admin holding `console.alerts.manage` resolves an alert by hand (idempotent — a condition
still firing reopens on the next evaluator tick).

204.description: Resolved, and audited. Idempotent. A condition still present opens again on the evaluator's next pass

get.summary: Lists a tenant's API keys as metadata only — never a secret (super-admin only).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose keys to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's keys, as an array: each with `id`, `store_id` (absent for a tenant-wide key), `scopes`, `revoked` and `expires_at_ms`. Never a token or a secret

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: Provisions a new scoped per-tenant API key and returns the one-time token (super-admin only).
post.description:
Behind the session guard. Mints a CSPRNG id and secret at the edge, [`issue`]s the key, and
persists it (storing only the secret's hash). The token in the `201` body is the only time the
secret is visible.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`; `store_id` to bind the key to one store, or absent for a tenant-wide key (a store's own sync credential must name its store); `scopes`, the only things the key may do: `read_rollups`, `read_config`, `manage_devices`, `place_orders`, `relay_orders` or `publish_events`; and `expires_at_ms`, or absent for a key that never expires

201.description: Provisioned. The body carries the key's `id` and its `token`, `pos_<id>_<secret>`. The token is returned exactly once — only a hash of the secret is stored. The audit entry records the scopes and the expiry, never the token

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID, a scope is unknown, or expires_at_ms is out of range

503.description: The key store or the entropy source is unavailable

delete.summary:
Revokes an API key by id (super-admin only). `204` whether or not a live key was found — revoking
is idempotent, and telling the caller which it was is a needless enumeration signal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's id, the ULID half of its token

204.description: No live key has that id any more. Idempotent: the answer is the same whether a live key was found, so it reveals nothing, and only a revocation that retired one is audited

400.description: id is not a ULID

get.summary:
A super-admin lists assignments, by exactly one of four selectors: everyone who works at a store
(`?store_id=` — every assignment that reaches it: its own, its groups' and the tenant's), all a
person holds (`?employee_id=`), those naming a store group (`?store_group_id=`), or those that
reach every store (`?scope_kind=ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`). Each row says its scope. Behind
[`ConsolePermission::ReadPeople`], the roster's gate: each row names the person it grants
([`Assignment`]).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose assignments to list (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: Everyone who works at this store: every assignment that reaches it, its own, its groups' and the tenant's

parameters.name: store_group_id
parameters.description: The assignments naming this store group

parameters.name: scope_kind
parameters.description: `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`: the assignments that reach every store

200.description: The assignments, as an array. Each says its scope and names the person it grants, by name and staff code

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID; not exactly one of store_id, employee_id, store_group_id and scope_kind is sent; the id sent is not a ULID; or scope_kind is not `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT`

post.summary:
A super-admin assigns an employee with a role, at one store, a store group or every store of the
tenant ([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 3; [`requested_scope`] reads which). Audited `assignment.create` with the ids and the
scope ([`assignment_audit`]).
post.description:
Each id is checked before anything is written, because the schema declares no foreign keys
under row-level security and leaves the check to this route (ADR-0070). An employee, store,
group or role the tenant does not have is `404` — another tenant's group included — and one it
has archived is `409` (decision 7): a grant to a retired person, store or group would publish
nobody, and one with a retired role would grant nothing, while the console showed it as a grant.
Each refusal names the field that carried the id. A person who already holds an assignment
there is `409` too ([`already_assigned`]), and nothing is written, audited or published.

An assignment to one store publishes as before, when someone presses publish, and answers `201`
with its id. One to a group or to every store publishes the `permissions` node at once to every
store it reaches — the open stores the group holds, or every open store of the tenant, read
before the write — and answers `201` with its id and each store's outcome (`stores`).

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `employee_id`, `role_template_id`, and where the role is held: a `store_id` for one store, a `store_group_id` for every store the group holds, or `scope_kind` `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_TENANT` for every store of the tenant (ADR-0158 decision 3)

201.description: Assigned. The body is `{ "id": … }`. An assignment to a group or to every store is published at once to every open store it reaches, and the body also carries `stores`, each with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`. One to a single store is published when someone publishes

400.description: An id is absent or not a ULID, the scope is named twice or not at all, or scope_kind is not one the route accepts

404.description: The tenant has no such employee, store, store group or role. The error names the field that carried the id

409.description: The employee, store, store group or role is archived, or the person already holds an assignment there. Nothing is written

503.description: The people store, the registry, the store groups or the entropy source is unavailable

delete.summary:
A super-admin removes an assignment — offboarding a person from where it reached. Audited
`assignment.remove` when a row was actually removed, with the ids and the scope it bound; a no-op
removal records nothing.
delete.description:
The removal publishes the `permissions` node at once to every store the assignment reached — its
store, the open stores its group holds, or every open store of the tenant — so the person cannot
sign in there a moment longer
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and answers `200` with each store's outcome.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: Removed, and every store the assignment reached is published to at once, so the person cannot sign in there a moment longer (ADR-0158 decision 7): `stores` lists each store with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`, which `POST /admin/people/publish` retries

400.description: tenant_id or assignment_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no assignment with that id

503.description: The people store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

get.summary: A super-admin (any console role) reads the audit trail, filtered by the query string.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: One tenant's entries (a 26-character ULID). Absent, the fleet-wide trail, tenant-global entries included

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Only entries about this kind of record, such as `store`

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only entries with this action, such as `store.update`

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Only entries at or after this instant (Unix ms)

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Only entries at or before this instant (Unix ms)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Without `offset`, the most recent this many entries (default 200, larger values read as 500). With `offset`, the page size, 1 to 500, refused rather than clamped

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Asks for a page: how many entries to skip, 0 to 100000

200.description: Without `offset`, the newest matching entries as an array; with it, a page: `items`, `total`, `limit` and `offset`. Each entry has `id`, `tenant_id`, the acting administrator's id, email and role, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `before`, `after`, `request_id` and `at_ms`. An entry about an employee carries the person's staff code only for a role holding console.people.read (ADR-0158 decision 9)

400.description: tenant_id is not a ULID; limit or offset is not an integer in range; or order is sent without offset or is not one the route accepts

get.summary: A super-admin lists a tenant's brands.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose brands to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's brands, as an array: `brand_id`, `tenant_id`, `name` and `status`, each with its `etag`

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: A super-admin creates a brand under a tenant.

requestBody.description: The `tenant_id` the brand belongs to and its `name`

201.description: Created, active, with the id minted here. The body is the record and the ETag carries its version

400.description: tenant_id is not a ULID

503.description: The registry store or the entropy source is unavailable

patch.summary: A super-admin renames a brand and/or sets its status.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the record was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: The `tenant_id` that owns the brand, and its `name` and `status` (`active` or `archived`) as they should now stand

200.description: Updated. The body is the record and the ETag carries its new version

400.description: brand_id or tenant_id is not a ULID, status is not `active` or `archived`, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no brand with that id

412.description: The brand changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

get.summary: A super-admin lists a tenant's authored campaigns.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose campaigns to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's campaigns as authored, each with its `etag`. A campaign reaches a store only when the store's campaigns are published

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: A super-admin creates a campaign; the server mints its id.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `name`, `kind` (`item_level`, `combo`, `bill_level`, `voucher` or `manual`), `priority`, and optionally `exclusion_group`, then the `action` the edge's pricing engine applies, its `conditions` (channels, a daily schedule window and the rest) and `quota_remaining`, in the shape of `pos-proto`'s published campaign. The id is never sent: the server owns it

201.description: Created, with the id minted here. The body is the campaign and the ETag carries its version. Audited with its name, kind and priority, never its discount terms

400.description: An id is not a ULID; name is blank; a schedule minute is outside the day; a channel is unknown; or a percentage or amount off is negative

409.description: A campaign with the minted id already exists

503.description: The campaign store or the entropy source is unavailable

get.summary: A super-admin reads one campaign by id.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The campaign as authored, with its `etag` field — the token a PUT must send back as If-Match

400.description: tenant_id or campaign_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no campaign with that id

put.summary: A super-admin updates a campaign in place, by the path id.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the campaign was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `name`, `kind` (`item_level`, `combo`, `bill_level`, `voucher` or `manual`), `priority`, and optionally `exclusion_group`, then the `action` the edge's pricing engine applies, its `conditions` (channels, a daily schedule window and the rest) and `quota_remaining`, in the shape of `pos-proto`'s published campaign. The id is never sent: the server owns it

200.description: Updated. The body is the campaign and the ETag carries its new version. Audited with its name, kind and priority before and after, never its discount terms

400.description: An id is not a ULID; name is blank; a schedule minute is outside the day; a channel is unknown; a percentage or amount off is negative; or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no campaign with that id

412.description: The campaign changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

delete.summary: A super-admin deletes a campaign by id.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

204.description: Deleted, and audited. A store keeps running it until its campaigns are next published

400.description: tenant_id or campaign_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no campaign with that id

get.summary: A super-admin lists a campaign's minted voucher codes.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many codes to return, 1 to 500. Absent, every code as an array rather than a page

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many codes to skip, 0 to 100000. Only with `limit`

200.description: Without `limit`, every code as an array; with it, a page: `items`, `total`, `limit` and `offset`. Each code has `voucher_id`, `code` and `status` (`active`, `redeemed` or `void`). Listing codes needs the manage permission, because a code carries redeemable value

400.description: tenant_id or campaign_id is absent or not a ULID, limit or offset is not an integer in range, or offset is sent without limit

post.summary: A super-admin mints a batch of voucher codes for a voucher-kind campaign.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and `count`, how many codes to mint, from 1 to 10000

201.description: Minted, as an array: each code's `voucher_id`, `code` and `status`, `active`. A code carries redeemable value; the audit entry records the count, never the codes

400.description: An id is not a ULID, count is out of range, or the campaign is not a voucher campaign

404.description: The tenant has no campaign with that id

503.description: The campaign store, the voucher store or the entropy source is unavailable

get.summary:
Serves the §10 capability catalogue for the console's form editor. Each flag says whether the
console offers it as a switch ([`offered`]).

200.description: The capability catalogue, the same for every tenant: `flags`, each with its `key`, `default_on`, `description` and `offered` (whether the console offers it as a switch); `presets`, each an `id` and the keys it turns on; and `rules`, the inter-flag rules a publish enforces

get.summary:
A super-admin lists a tenant's courses, **in service order**
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md)).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose courses to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's courses, as an array, each with its `etag`, in service order: by `sort` ascending, then by id (ADR-0130)

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: A super-admin creates a course; the id is minted here and returned once.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, the course's `name`, and `sort`, where it falls in the service sequence, ascending (absent is 0)

201.description: Created, active, with the id minted here. The body is the record and the ETag carries its version. Audited

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or name is blank

503.description: The catalog store or the entropy source is unavailable

patch.summary: A super-admin renames a course, moves it in the service sequence and/or archives it.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the record was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, and the course's `name`, `sort` and `status` (`active` or `archived`) as they should now stand

200.description: Updated. The body is the record and the ETag carries its new version. Audited

404.description: The tenant has no course with that id

412.description: The course changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

get.summary:
A super-admin exports a tenant's catalog items as CSV ([ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md),
Track M5). Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and audited — the entry records who exported
which domain and how many rows, never the row contents. No price is exported (prices are per-channel
placements, a deferred T2 export); this is the item master only.

200.description: `items.csv`, as a `text/csv` attachment: the header `menu_item_id,name,status,tax_class_id,item_category_id,item_subcategory_id,image_ref`, then one row per item. No price, no translation and no course. A name a spreadsheet would read as a formula is escaped. Audited by row count, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

500.description: The CSV could not be built

post.summary:
`POST /admin/catalog/import/items` — the confirm after a dry run: the valid rows are written and
the rejected ones are reported, never written.
post.description:
# Why a row can be applied and reported as applied, and the next one still fail

The rows are separate records and are written one at a time, so this is not a transaction and
does not pretend to be. What it does instead is report per row: a row whose write was refused
comes back as a rejection naming what happened, so re-importing the same file after fixing it is
safe — the rows that already landed are updates at their new version, and the rest are retried.
Wrapping the whole file in one transaction would mean one bad row discarding an operator's whole
afternoon, which is the behaviour the dry run exists to make unnecessary.

An update is conditional on the version read when the import began, so a row somebody else
changed in between is refused rather than silently overwritten
([ADR-0094](../../../docs/adr/0094-optimistic-concurrency-on-admin.md)).

Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and audited — the row counts, never the contents.

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, with the same header, as the raw request body. A row with a `menu_item_id` this tenant has updates that item; a row with none creates one; any other id is rejected, so a file cannot mint an item id. The format carries no price, translation or course, and an update keeps what it does not carry

200.description: Applied: the valid rows are written one at a time and the report is the dry run's, with any row whose write failed turned into a rejection naming why — `rows`, one per data row in file order, each with its `key` and its `action`: `create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`; and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. Not one transaction: re-importing the same file after a fix is safe. An update is conditional on the version read when the import began, so a row changed meanwhile is rejected rather than overwritten. Audited by counts, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or the body is not CSV or its header is not the export's

503.description: The catalog store or the entropy source is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /admin/catalog/import/items/dry-run` — what an item-master CSV **would** do, row by row,
writing nothing (roadmap-v3 **F15**, [ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md)).
post.description:
The file is the one `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, which is what makes the pair a
round-trip: export the master, edit it in a spreadsheet, bring it back. It carries no price —
a price is a per-channel placement — so neither the upload nor the report an operator reads can
carry one in clear text.

Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageCatalog`] and not audited, because it changes nothing.

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/catalog/export/items` writes, with the same header, as the raw request body. A row with a `menu_item_id` this tenant has updates that item; a row with none creates one; any other id is rejected, so a file cannot mint an item id. The format carries no price, translation or course, and an update keeps what it does not carry

200.description: What the file would do, writing nothing: `rows`, one per data row in file order, each with its `key` and its `action`: `create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`; and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. A row naming a tax class, category, sub-category or image the tenant does not have is rejected here, by row. Not audited

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or the body is not CSV or its header is not the export's

get.summary: A super-admin lists a tenant's item categories.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose item categories to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's item categories, as an array, each with its `etag`

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: A super-admin creates an item category; the id is minted here and returned once.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and the category's `name`

201.description: Created, active, with the id minted here. The body is the record and the ETag carries its version. Audited

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

patch.summary: A super-admin renames an item category and/or sets its status.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the record was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, and the category's `name` and `status` (`active` or `archived`) as they should now stand

200.description: Updated. The body is the record and the ETag carries its new version. Audited

being written: what the store is sent is checked against what it will hold. A store that cannot

`POST /admin/config/campaigns/preview` — the dry-run of the campaigns publish. Assembles the
tenant's authored campaigns into the `campaigns` node exactly as the publish route would, then
returns the merge patch it would apply to the store's effective document — without minting a
version, saving, or auditing (it changes nothing). `422` with the same violations a real publish
would reject the candidate with. Behind [`ConsolePermission::PublishConfig`], the same audience
that can actually publish. The diff is redacted for the caller's role, as the generic preview's
is ([`config_redacted_for`]): its staff, because it can carry the `permissions` node too, and
its prices, because the `campaigns` node it previews carries combo prices, discount amounts and
minimum-bill thresholds — which Ops, who may publish, does not read (S8).

post.summary:
`POST /admin/config/lease/bump` — issues this store's next lease generation and publishes it
([ADR-0108](../../../docs/adr/0108-the-lease-generation-is-authority.md)).
post.description:
This is the act of saying **"a different machine is the store now"**. One request does two things
that must not drift apart: it advances the authoritative counter in `store_lease`, and it
publishes the resulting number as the Store-layer `lease` node — the only rail that reaches a
till. The node is *derived* here, never authored: no route accepts a `lease` body, because a
generation a person could type would not be an authority.

A store's **first** bump lands on generation `0` and supersedes nobody — ADR-0049's "the first
lease a store ever issues is generation `0`" — so it is the act of putting a store under the
lease at all. Every bump after that supersedes whatever box holds the previous number: it stops
installing updates on its next config pull, and stays stopped across reboots, because the edge
takes its generation once and thereafter only compares.

Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageStores`] rather than `PublishOta`: replacing the machine that
*is* a store is store management, and the person who does it is the person who provisions
hardware, not the person who runs an upgrade campaign. The audit entry names the generation
issued, so "who replaced this box, and when" has an answer.

# The third thing that must not drift apart

[ADR-0110](../../../docs/adr/0110-edge-placement-is-a-deployment-axis.md) makes *where* the store
runs an attribute of the store, and this route the only writer of it. A body naming
`edge_placement` is a **move**; a body omitting it is a swap in place, and keeps whatever the
store had. Either way the value is written inside the bump's own statement, so a reader can never
catch the two disagreeing — which is not fussiness but the difference between a console that says
"Offline-capable: yes" about a hosted store and one that does not.

An explicit `EDGE_PLACEMENT_UNSPECIFIED` is refused rather than accepted as "no change". On the
wire that token means *this message did not say*, so a caller that sends it has said nothing in a
field that looks like it said something; omitting the field is how you mean that, and a refusal
that says so beats a request that appears to move a store and does not.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The lease generation the decision was made against, or `*` for a store never issued one. Required

No body names a generation: the server issues it

The new generation is published as the store's `lease` node, with the receipt floor beside it where the cloud has one (ADR-0149), and the box on the old generation stops installing updates. The body carries `config_version_id`. Audited with the generation issued

risk that no fact in this system implies

handover is in flight, because a machine that may hold the only copy of a night's sales is not

Publishes nothing, for the same reason settle does not.

post.summary: `POST /admin/config/preview` — what publishing this node to this store *would* change.
post.description:
# Why this exists when `/admin/config/campaigns/preview` already did

It did, for one node out of sixteen. Every other publish button in the console committed
blind: the operator pressed **Publish** and found out afterwards, from the store, whether the
document was what they meant (roadmap-v3 **F11**). Writing fifteen more preview routes by hand
would have been fifteen more chances for a preview to compile its node differently from the
publish it previews — a dry run that lies is worse than none.

So this route compiles through [`BatchNode`], the same registry ADR-0122's batch publish fans
out, which delegates to the very `*_nodes` function each single-store route calls. A preview
cannot drift from its publish because it is not a second copy of it. The nodes the registry does
not carry have no preview here, and deliberately: `locale` and `store_profile` are per-store by
definition (ADR-0122 §4), so there is no tenant-wide document to compile.

# Whom the diff names

A `permissions` preview carries the store's roster: each member's name, staff code and PIN
hash. Publishing that node shows nobody any of them, and `PublishConfig` is Ops's permission
too, so the diff gets a config read's treatment ([`config_redacted_for`]): never a PIN hash, and
a name or code only for a role holding [`ConsolePermission::ReadPeople`]
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)). Every
node's preview is redacted, not only that one's: a store with layers and no published version
has nothing to diff against, so the diff of any node is the whole document, staff included.

# Whom the diff prices

A `menu` preview carries the store's price book, and a `campaigns` or `fees` one the promotions'
and fees' amounts. `PublishConfig` is Ops's, `ReadRevenue` is not, and the config read already
withholds those nodes from Ops (S8) — so the diff withholds them too ([`config_redacted_for`]).

It is redacted *after* it is computed, never before. Diffing redacted documents would answer
`unchanged: true` to a PIN reset or a rename, and an operator told that nothing would change
would not publish the change the till is waiting for.

Mints no version, saves nothing, audits nothing. `422` carries the violations a real publish
would refuse the candidate with, verbatim.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `store_id`, `node` (one of the nodes a batch publish can compile), and `arguments`, that node's own publish body without the tenant and store. Nothing is written

200.description: What publishing the node would change: `node`; `from_version_id`, the version the diff is against, or `null` for a store never published to; `diff`, the merge patch (RFC 7386) the publish would apply; and `unchanged`. The node is compiled by the publish's own code, so the preview cannot differ from it. The diff never shows a staff PIN hash; shows a name or staff code only to a role holding console.people.read; and shows the priced nodes (`menu`, `campaigns`, `fees`) only to a role holding console.reports.revenue, so Ops, who may publish, is not shown prices. `unchanged` is computed before redaction. Not audited

A super-admin publishes a store's per-marketplace policies as its `vendors` node. Each policy's
availability must be a recognised value; the live loop that pushes it to a marketplace is deferred.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and `store_id`, then `policies`, one per delivery marketplace: its name, whether the store takes its orders, the store's availability to it, and the preparation time it quotes while the store is busy

200.description: Published as the store's `vendors` node on its Store layer. The body carries `config_version_id`, which the store pulls on its next sync. Audited with the node's value

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID, an availability is not a recognised value, or a value needs a recorded confirmation first (ADR-0169)

412.description: Every attempt to write the store's configuration lost a race with another publish: try again

422.description: The store's configuration would not validate with the node

get.summary: A super-admin lists the compiled country modules.

200.description: Every country module this build carries, as an array: `code`, `display_name`, `currency_code` and `currency_exponent`, `default_language`, the number format (`decimal_separator`, `group_separator`, `digits_per_group`), `default_retention_days`, and the till facts a store's settings start from: `prices_include_tax`, `cash_rounding_increment` and `cash_denominations`, in the currency's minor units (ADR-0105). Fixed when the server starts; the same for every tenant

get.summary: A super-admin lists a tenant's pending device proposals — the approval queue.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose devices to list (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: Only this store's devices (a 26-character ULID). Absent, the tenant's whole fleet

200.description: The devices, as an array: each with `id`, `store_id`, `kind`, `name`, `address`, `status` and `version`, and once approved its `connection`, `station_id`, print agent, drawer mark, paper, and a till's receipt printer, receipt languages and opening float, where set

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, store_id is not a ULID, or status is not one of the three

post.summary:
A super-admin picks (or clears) the print agent for an approved device
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)).
post.description:
Behind `ManageDevices` with an `If-Match`
([ADR-0094](../../../docs/adr/0094-console-optimistic-concurrency.md)) and an audit entry: two
managers picking different agents for one printer is the ordinary race, and last-write-wins would
leave the loser believing a decision that is not in the database.

It deliberately does **not** check that the id names a terminal. Resolvability is a property of
the set being published — the terminal may be created after this pick — so the check lives in
[`admin_publish_devices`], which sees the whole node at once and is the last gate before a store
hears about any of it.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version the device was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and `agent_device_id`, the terminal whose print agent writes this printer's bytes (ADR-0112), or `null` for the store's edge to open the printer's address itself. Whether the id names a terminal is checked when the devices are published, since the terminal may be created after the pick

204.description: Saved, and audited. It reaches the store on the next devices publish

400.description: An id is not a ULID, the device names itself as its agent, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no approved device with that id

412.description: The device changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

post.summary: A super-admin approves a pending proposal.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: connection
parameters.description: How the device is attached: `usb`, `network` or `serial` (ADR-0100). Required: discovery cannot find it out, and it decides whether a cash drawer may be opened

parameters.name: station_id
parameters.description: The kitchen station the device serves (a 26-character ULID). Absent, it is the counter's receipt printer

204.description: No proposal with that id is pending any more. Idempotent: the answer is the same whether one was, and only an approval that acted is audited. The device reaches the store on the next `POST /admin/devices/publish`

400.description: tenant_id, id or station_id is not a ULID, or connection is absent or not one of the three

post.summary:
A super-admin ticks (or clears) **Cash drawer attached** on an approved printer
([ADR-0165](../../../docs/adr/0165-cash-paid-in-and-out-is-counted-in-the-drawer-and-a-no-sale-opening-needs-a-manager.md)
decision 4).
post.description:
The agent pick's guards, for the agent pick's reasons: `ManageDevices`, an `If-Match`, and an
audit entry. The mark decides whether a drawer full of cash can be sprung from the till, so who
set it, and when, is worth a row. It reaches a store on the next devices publish, as every other
fact about a device does.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version the device was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and `drawer_attached`, whether a cash drawer is wired to the printer's kick port (ADR-0165 decision 4). It decides whether the till can open a drawer of cash

204.description: Saved, and audited. It reaches the store on the next devices publish

400.description: An id is not a ULID, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no approved device with that id

412.description: The device changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

post.summary:
A super-admin says what a till's drawer opens with by default
([ADR-0167](../../../docs/adr/0167-a-till-has-its-own-cash-drawer.md) decision 4).
post.description:
The receipts' guards, for the receipts' reasons: `ManageDevices`, an `If-Match`, and an audit
entry, since the float is the cash the Shift screen proposes a till's drawer start with. The
bounds are `shift.opening_float_minor`'s, which pos-proto holds, so a till is never given a
float the store could not be; the edge reads one outside them as the store's anyway.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version the terminal was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`; and `opening_float_minor`, a whole amount in the store currency's minor unit from `0` to `1000000000`, the bounds of `shift.opening_float_minor`, or `null` or absent for that setting's float. It is the till's whole float state, so a float left out is the store's again

204.description: Saved. It reaches the store on the next devices publish, `POST /admin/devices/publish`, and prefills the float the till's drawer is started on; an edge older than 0.14.1 ignores it and prefills the store's

400.description: The device is not a terminal (`id`, `WRONG_KIND`), the float is outside its bounds (`opening_float_minor`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`), an id is not a ULID, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no approved device with that id

412.description: The terminal changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

post.summary:
A super-admin says what paper an approved printer takes and whether it cuts it
([ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 2).
post.description:
The drawer mark's guards, for the drawer mark's reasons: `ManageDevices`, an `If-Match`, and an
audit entry. The width decides how a receipt is laid out and how wide a raster is drawn, and the
cutter whether a printer is sent a cut, so who set them is worth a row. They reach a store on the
next devices publish, as every other fact about a device does. `PAPER_WIDTH_UNSPECIFIED` is
refused with every token this release does not know: it is what an older reader takes a newer
paper to be, never a choice.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version the printer was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`; `paper_width`, one of `PAPER_WIDTH_MILLIMETRES_80` (42 characters a line and a 576-dot raster), `PAPER_WIDTH_MILLIMETRES_80_COLUMNS_48` (48 characters, 576 dots) and `PAPER_WIDTH_MILLIMETRES_58` (32 characters, 384 dots); and `cuts_paper`, `false` for a printer with no cutter. A printer nobody has set prints as 80 mm paper with a cutter

204.description: Saved. It reaches the store on the next devices publish, `POST /admin/devices/publish`

400.description: `paper_width` is not one of the three, an id is not a ULID, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no approved device with that id

412.description: The device changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

post.summary:
A super-admin says which printer a till's receipts, receipt copies and pre-bills go to, and the
languages they print in
([ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 4).
post.description:
The paper's guards, for the paper's reasons: `ManageDevices`, an `If-Match`, and an audit entry.
Unlike an agent pick, the printer is checked here, against the tenant's approved devices: it must
be a printer of the terminal's own store that serves no station, because a kitchen's printer is
for its tickets and another store's is in another building. What the check cannot see is a
printer that leaves the approved set later: the publish then leaves that till printing at the
store's receipt printer.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version the terminal was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`; `receipt_printer_id`, an approved printer of the terminal's store that serves no station; `receipt_language`, one of `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_DISPLAY`, `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_COUNTRY`, `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_VI` and `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_EN`; and `receipt_second_language`, one of `RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_NONE`, `RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_VI` and `RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_EN`. Each is `null` or absent for the store's: its receipt printer, `printing.receipt_language` and `printing.receipt_second_language`. The three are the till's whole receipt state, so a field left out is the store's again

204.description: Saved. It reaches the store on the next devices publish, `POST /admin/devices/publish`; an edge older than 0.14.1 ignores it. A device paired at the store prints by it once it is bound to the terminal, `POST /api/print/agent`

400.description: The device is not a terminal (`id`, `WRONG_KIND`), `receipt_printer_id` is not an approved device of its store (`UNKNOWN_REFERENCE`) or not a printer serving no station (`WRONG_KIND`), a language is not one of its choices, an id is not a ULID, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no approved device with that id

412.description: The terminal changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

post.summary: A super-admin rejects a pending proposal.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

204.description: No proposal with that id is pending any more. Idempotent: the answer is the same whether one was, and only a rejection that acted is audited

400.description: tenant_id or id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary:
Compiles a store's **approved** devices into its `devices` config node and versions it
([ADR-0100](../../../docs/adr/0100-receipt-and-ticket-printing.md)).
post.description:
The same load→compile→write→version shape as the floor publish beside it, onto the `devices` key.
A device whose stored `kind` or `connection` this build does not know keeps its token through
`Open` rather than failing the publish — the store on the other end applies the same rule, and a
node that refused to compile over one unfamiliar device would take a shop's receipt printer with
it.

A proposal with **no** connection is skipped, not published as a guess. That state is only
reachable for a row approved before ADR-0100 (the route now requires it), and publishing it as
`network` would silently disable the cash drawer on a USB printer. Skipping is visible: the
response says how many were published and how many were held back.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and the `store_id` whose approved devices to compile into its `devices` node (ADR-0100)

200.description: Published. The body carries `config_version_id`, the version the store syncs, `device_count`, and `skipped_count`: approved devices held back because no connection was ever recorded for them, which are not published as a guess. Audited

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is absent or not a ULID

412.description: Every attempt to write the store's configuration lost a race with another publish: try again

422.description: A printer names a print agent that is not a terminal among the store's approved devices, naming both, or the store's configuration would not validate with the node

503.description: The device store or the configuration store is unreachable

post.summary:
A super-admin creates an approved `terminal` device
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)).
post.description:
Behind `ManageDevices` rather than `PublishConfig`, and audited, because this is the human gate:
nothing on a LAN announces itself as a till, so there is no proposal for an operator to approve
and the named admin creating the entry is the decision ADR-0041 protects. It carries no
`connection` and no address — the agent connects outbound to the edge, and nothing dials a
terminal.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, the `store_id` the terminal stands in, and its `name`, what an operator recognises it by. A terminal is never discovered, so there is no proposal to approve: creating it is the decision (ADR-0112). It has no address, because nothing dials a terminal

201.description: Created, approved. The body carries the terminal's `id`, what a printer names to make it its print agent, and `status`. Audited

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID, or name is blank

503.description: The device store or the entropy source is unavailable

get.summary:
A super-admin lists a tenant's employees. Behind [`ConsolePermission::ReadPeople`]: every row
carries a person's name and staff code.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose employees to list (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many employees to return, 1 to 500. Absent, the whole roster is returned as an array rather than a page

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many employees to skip, 0 to 100000. Only with `limit`

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A case-insensitive substring the person's name or staff code must contain. Only with `limit`

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` (the default) or `desc`, inverting `sort`'s direction. Only with `limit`

200.description: Without `limit`, every employee as an array; with it, a page: `items`, `total`, `limit` and `offset`. Each employee has `employee_id`, `tenant_id`, `code`, `name`, `status` and `has_pin` — never the PIN or its hash

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID; limit or offset is not an integer in range; offset, q, sort or order is sent without limit; or sort or order is not one the route accepts

post.summary:
A super-admin creates an employee (no PIN yet). Audited `employee.create` with id/code/status —
never the name. A staff code the tenant already uses is `409` ([`code_in_use`]), and nothing is
written or audited.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, the staff `code` the person types to sign in, unique within the tenant, and their `name`. No PIN: it is set with `PUT …/pin`

201.description: Created. The body is `{ "id": … }` and the ETag carries the new employee's version. The employee starts active

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or code or name is blank

409.description: The tenant already uses that staff code. The error names the `code` field, never the code

503.description: The people store or the entropy source is unavailable

get.summary:
A super-admin reads one employee within its tenant. Behind [`ConsolePermission::ReadPeople`],
like the list.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that employs them (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The employee, with an ETag carrying the version it was read at — the token a PATCH must send back as If-Match

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

patch.summary:
A super-admin renames an employee and/or sets their status. Audited `employee.update` with
before/after id/code/status — never the name.
patch.description:
Archiving the person publishes the `permissions` node at once to every store they are assigned
to, so they cannot sign in at any of them a moment longer
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and the answer is then `200` with each store's outcome. Any other update — a
rename, or restoring an archived person — publishes as before, and answers `204`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the employee was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, the `name` and the `status` (`active` or `archived`) as they should now stand. The staff code cannot be changed

200.description: Archived. The person is taken off every store they were assigned to at once (ADR-0158 decision 7): `stores` lists each store with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`, which `POST /admin/people/publish` retries. The ETag carries the new version

204.description: Updated: a rename, or restoring an archived person. Nothing is published until someone publishes. The ETag carries the new version

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID, name is blank, status is not `active` or `archived`, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

412.description: The employee changed since you read it: re-read them and try again

503.description: The people store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

put.summary:
A super-admin sets or resets an employee's PIN. The digits are hashed with Argon2id here and never
returned, stored raw, or **audited** — the entry records only that a PIN was set, by whom
(ADR-0070).
put.description:
A PIN has at least the digits the tenant's `session.pin_min_length` asks for, four where it asks
for none, and at most eight (ADR-0160). This is the one place the minimum is applied: the edge
holds only a PIN's hash. Raising the minimum leaves a PIN already set as it is. If the tenant's
settings cannot be read, the PIN is refused rather than held to four.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id` and the `pin`: digits only, at least the tenant's `session.pin_min_length` (four where it sets none) and at most eight. The PIN is hashed at once and is never returned, stored in the clear, logged or audited (ADR-0070)

204.description: Set. A store learns the new PIN when its people are next published

400.description: tenant_id or employee_id is absent or not a ULID, or the PIN is not digits of an allowed length

404.description: The tenant has no employee with that id

503.description: The people store, the settings store or the entropy source is unavailable

get.summary: `GET /admin/fees` — the rules a tenant has written, at every scope.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose rules to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: Every rule the tenant has written, at every scope: the scope and the id it was written for, the rule with the item categories it names, and who last wrote it when

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

503.description: The fee rule store is unreachable

put.summary: `PUT /admin/fees` — writes a fee at one scope and republishes every store it reaches.

requestBody.description: As a POST, with the rule's fee_id: the fee to write at this scope. Written where it is, the rule replaces it; written at a narrower scope, it overrides the broader one for the stores that scope reaches

200.description: Written, and every store it reaches republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a POST

400.description: As a POST, or the fee_id is absent

404.description: The tenant has no such brand or store

422.description: As a POST

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary: `POST /admin/fees` — writes a new fee, minting its id, and republishes every store it reaches.

requestBody.description: The tenant, the scope (FEE_SCOPE_TENANT, _BRAND or _STORE), the id it is for, and the rule without a fee_id: code, display_name and its translations, kind (FEE_KIND_PERCENT with a rate, or FEE_KIND_AMOUNT_PER_BILL or _PER_UNIT with an amount), channels, item_scope with menu_item_ids and item_category_ids, base_discounted, base_tax_inclusive, tax (with a tax_class_id for FEE_TAX_TAX_CLASS), waivable and active

404.description: The tenant has no such brand or store

422.description: A store the rule takes effect at could not apply it: an amount in another currency than the store's, or a tax class it has no rate for; or the store already runs another fee with this code; or an item list names nothing on the menu of any store it takes effect at

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

delete.summary: `DELETE /admin/fees` — removes a rule at one scope and republishes every store it reached.

parameters.name: scope_id
parameters.description: The tenant, brand or store the rule was written for

200.description: Removed, and every store it reached republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a write. A store that ran it runs the fee's broader rule if there is one, and otherwise no longer charges it

400.description: An id is not a ULID or the scope is not a scope

404.description: No rule is written there

422.description: A store would then run the fee's broader rule, and could not apply it, or runs another fee with its code

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

get.summary: `GET /admin/fees/effective` — the fees one store runs, and why.

200.description: Every fee the store runs, in the order it is sent them: the scope and id its rule was written at, the rule as written, the rule as the store is sent it with its categories compiled into items, and any reason the store cannot apply it. publishable is false when one cannot be applied, in which case a publish leaves the store as it is

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary:
`POST /admin/fees/preview` — a sample bill at one store with rules in place, before they are
written ([ADR-0159](../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md): "the console previews a
sample bill before publishing").
post.description:
A read: it writes nothing and publishes nothing, so it stands behind the fee reads' permission.
It resolves the store's rules with the ones sent in place, compiles them as a publish would, and
assembles the bill with [`crate::fees::sample_bill`], which prices each line and adds it up with
`pos_core`'s own functions, from the store's own published menu, tax table and rounding.

requestBody.description: The tenant, a store, the sales channel (dine-in when absent), the rules as they would be written — each with its scope and scope_id and the rule as a PUT sends it, its fee_id absent for a fee not created yet — and the sample bill's lines, each a menu_item_id from the store's menu and a quantity of 1 to 999. From 1 to 50 lines, and at most 20 rules

200.description: The sample bill as the store would assemble it with those rules in place: each line priced from its menu, each fee charged with its tax and the parts of it taxed at each class, the tax per class, the cash rounding and the total due. Nothing is written or published

400.description: An id is not a ULID, the channel or a scope is not one, a rule is refused as a write would refuse it, or there are no lines, too many lines or rules, or a quantity out of range

404.description: The tenant has no such store, brand or store a rule is for

422.description: The store could not assemble the bill: it has no locale, tax table or menu published (NOT_PUBLISHED), a line is not on its menu for the channel (NOT_ON_MENU), not available (NOT_AVAILABLE) or has no tax rate (TAX_RATE_NOT_CONFIGURED), or a rule it would run cannot apply there

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry, the catalog or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary: `POST /admin/fees/publish` — republishes the fees of one store, or of every store of the tenant.
post.description:
A write republishes every store it reaches by itself. What it cannot see is a change elsewhere
that changes what a store is sent: a store given another brand, or an item added to or taken
out of a category a rule names, which is compiled into items when the fees are published. A
menu publish brings a store's fees along with it; this publishes them without one.

requestBody.description: The tenant, and optionally one store. Without a store, every store of the tenant is republished

200.description: Each store's rules resolved, compiled and republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a write

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The fee rule store, the registry or the catalog is unreachable

get.summary: A super-admin (any console role) lists a tenant's whole fleet, online/offline derived at read.

parameters.description: The tenant whose stores to list (a 26-character ULID)

get.summary: A super-admin reads one floor area, with the version it was read at.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant the record belongs to (a 26-character ULID)

patch.summary: A super-admin sets a floor area's whole new state, conditional on the version it was read at.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the record was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

post.summary: A super-admin uploads one release artifact: the bare executable, plus its minisign signature.
post.description:
Idempotent by [`admit_artifact`]'s rule — re-uploading the same release/target with identical
bytes answers `200` rather than failing, so a re-run of a release step does not wedge; different
bytes for a release a ring may already have installed are refused, because a version that can
change under a fleet is not a version.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: The release the bytes are, spelled bare as a rollout's `target_version` names it, without a leading `v`. Required

parameters.name: arch
parameters.description: The target triple the executable is built for. Required

parameters.name: x-pos-minisig
parameters.description: minisign's signature over these exact bytes: the second line of the `.minisig` file, as base64. Required

requestBody.description: The bare release executable, not the release archive: the edge installs the bytes it is handed, so the signature has to cover these (ADR-0088). `docs/release-runbook.md` step 5 gives the exact request

200.description: Already hosted with these exact bytes: the release is unchanged, so a re-run of a release step does not fail. The body is as for 201. Audited

201.description: Hosted: the signature, then the executable, are stored, and only then the release is recorded. The body carries `release`, `arch`, `size_bytes` and `sha256`. Audited

400.description: release or arch is absent or unusable; the body is empty; or the signature header is absent, not base64, or not a minisign signature. An absent query parameter is refused by the framework, without the error envelope

409.description: This release is already hosted for this target with different bytes. A version a ring may have installed does not change

413.description: The executable is over 128 MiB. Answered by the server's body limit, without the error envelope

500.description: The storage keys could not be composed

503.description: The object store or the release registry is unreachable: send the same upload again later

post.summary: A super-admin points the cloud at a release, and it fetches every pair the forge holds for it.
post.description:
The button behind `docs/release-runbook.md` step 5: instead of downloading six files and running
three `curl`s with a console cookie, the operator names the version. What the cloud *holds*
afterwards is identical either way — the same blobs, the same rows, the same immutability rule —
because both doors go through [`admit_release_artifact`].

Not a transaction. Each target is admitted on its own, so a refusal on the third leaves the first
two hosted; that is the same grain the upload has always had (one call per target), and the
refusal names which target stopped it.

requestBody.description: `release`: the version to fetch, spelled bare, without a leading `v`. The cloud tries the release workflow's tag with and without one

200.description: Every signed executable the release publishes is hosted. The body carries `release`, `tag`, the release source's tag it came from, and `artifacts`: for each, `arch`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, `asset`, and `outcome`, `recorded` or `already_hosted`. Audited

422.description: The release carries no signed executable, or an asset is too large or not what it claims to be

500.description: The storage keys could not be composed

503.description: The release source, the object store or the release registry is unreachable

get.summary:
Which targets a release is hosted for — what an operator checks before promoting it, and what the
promote guard consults on their behalf.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: The release, spelled bare, without a leading `v`

200.description: `release` and `artifacts`: for each target it is hosted for, `arch`, `size_bytes`, `sha256` and `recorded_at_ms`. An empty list means the release is not hosted, and a rollout naming it is refused

400.description: The release cannot name a hosted release

get.summary:
`GET /admin/ota/releases/{release}/installer?store_id=&cloud=` — a hosted release's Windows
executable, named as that store's one-file installer
([ADR-0141](../../../docs/adr/0141-the-console-hands-out-the-installer-by-name.md)).
get.description:
**The bytes are the release's own.** Nothing is appended or rewritten: the store and the cloud
travel in the file *name*, which is what lets the minisign signature over these bytes keep
verifying, and what makes the file safe to hand out — the name carries a store id and a host,
neither of them a secret, and the credential still arrives only through activation.

**`console.data.read`**, like the list beside it: this reads what the cloud hosts. It writes
nothing and provisions nothing — a box it installs is unactivated until somebody with
`console.devices.manage` mints it a code.

**The cloud's host comes from the caller**, not from the `Host` header. The console passes the
address its own browser is showing, the same value it writes into every generated installer;
behind a reverse proxy the `Host` a handler sees can be the upstream's, and a file naming
`127.0.0.1` would install a store that dials itself.

Buffered, as the store-facing serve route is ([`read_artifact_blobs`]): a download is a person
at a console, one file at a time.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: The release, spelled bare, without a leading `v`

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store the installer is for (a 26-character ULID), written into the file's name. Required

parameters.name: cloud
parameters.description: The cloud the store will dial, as the console's browser shows it: a host, or a host and port. Written into the file's name. Required

parameters.name: arch
parameters.description: A Windows target triple. Absent means the default Windows build

200.description: The release's Windows executable, byte for byte, as an `application/octet-stream` attachment named for the store and the cloud. Nothing is written into the bytes, so the release's signature still verifies; the store's credential arrives only through activation

400.description: The release cannot name a hosted release; store_id is absent or not a ULID; cloud is absent or cannot be written into a file name; or arch is not a target triple or not a Windows build

404.description: The release is not hosted for this target

500.description: The release is recorded but its executable is missing from the object store

503.description: The release registry or the object store is unreachable

get.summary:
The `pos-core` permission catalogue (§9), for the console's role editor to offer. Behind `Read` and

tree — the same load→compile→write→version shape as [`admin_publish_menu`], onto the `permissions`

200.description: Published. The body is `{ "config_version_id": … }`, the configuration version the store syncs. The node carries each assigned person's PIN hash for the store to verify against; the audit entry records only the version and the staff count

[ADR-0067](../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md) slice 6. Self-service, so it is

A super-admin creates a role template. Both permission sets are validated against the catalogue
([`granted_with_approval`]). Audited `role.create` with id, name, both sets and the ceiling (a
role name is not PII).

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `name`, `permissions` (granted directly), `permissions_with_approval` (granted only with a direct holder's approval, each PIN-flagged; absent is none) and `discount_ceiling_minor` (how much the role may discount without a manager, in the currency's minor unit; absent is no ceiling, which a store reads as zero). Every id must be in `GET /admin/people/permissions`, and none may be in both lists

201.description: Created. The body is `{ "id": … }` and the ETag carries the new role's version

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID; name is blank; a permission id is unknown, not PIN-flagged where granted with approval, or in both lists; or the ceiling is negative

get.summary: A super-admin reads one role template within its tenant.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The role template, with an ETag carrying the version it was read at — the token a PATCH must send back as If-Match

400.description: tenant_id or role_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no role with that id

patch.summary:
A super-admin updates a role template's name, permission sets, ceiling and status. Audited
`role.update` with what was written, both sets included ([`granted_with_approval`]).
patch.description:
An archived role grants nothing, so archiving one publishes the `permissions` node at once to
every store where someone holds it
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and the answer is then `200` with each store's outcome. Any other update — a
rename, a changed permission set or ceiling, or restoring the role — publishes as before, and
answers `204`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the role was read at (ADR-0094). Required; a wildcard is refused

requestBody.description: The role as it should now stand: `tenant_id`, `name`, `permissions`, `discount_ceiling_minor` and `status` (`active` or `archived`), and optionally `permissions_with_approval` — absent, the role keeps what it grants with approval, less anything `permissions` now grants directly

200.description: Archived. An archived role grants nothing, so every store where someone holds it is published to at once (ADR-0158 decision 7): `stores` lists each store with its `outcome`, `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_APPLIED` with its `config_version_id` or `PERMISSIONS_PUBLISH_FAILED`, which `POST /admin/people/publish` retries. The ETag carries the new version

204.description: Updated: a rename, a changed permission set or ceiling, or restoring the role. Nothing is published until someone publishes. The ETag carries the new version

400.description: tenant_id or role_id is absent or not a ULID; name is blank; a permission id is unknown, not PIN-flagged where granted with approval, or in both lists; status is not `active` or `archived`; the ceiling is negative; or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The tenant has no role with that id

412.description: The role changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

503.description: The people store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

get.summary: Confirms the caller holds a live super-admin session.
get.description:
The guard every other `/admin` route stands behind, exposed here as a `204`/`401` "am I signed
in?" check for the admin UI.

204.description: The session is live. The guard every other /admin route stands behind, exposed as an "am I signed in?" check

401.description: No session cookie, or it names no live session

get.summary:
`GET /admin/sessions` — the acting admin's own live sessions, newest first, with the current one
flagged. Self-service: available to any authenticated admin regardless of role (an admin always
manages their own sessions), so it is gated by the plain session guard, not a
[`ConsolePermission`].

200.description: The acting administrator's own live sessions, newest first, as an array: each with `id`, an opaque revocation handle (never the session token, and not reversible to it), the `ip` and `user_agent` it was signed in from where known, `created_at_ms`, `expires_at_ms`, and `current` for the session making this request. Any signed-in administrator, whatever their role

post.summary:
`POST /admin/sessions/revoke-others` — revoke every one of the acting admin's sessions except the
one making this request ("sign out everywhere else").

204.description: Every session of the acting administrator except the one making this request is revoked: signed out everywhere else

delete.summary:
`DELETE /admin/sessions/{id}` — revoke one of the acting admin's own sessions by its handle.
Scoped to the caller, so an admin can only revoke a session that is theirs: an unknown or
other-owned handle is a `404`, never a cross-admin revocation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session's handle, as `GET /admin/sessions` lists it

204.description: Revoked. The session can no longer be used

400.description: id is not a session handle

404.description: The acting administrator has no session with that handle. Another administrator's session is not found either: a session can be revoked only by its owner

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose values to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: Every value the tenant has written: the setting, the scope and the id it was written for, the value and when

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

requestBody.description: The tenant, the setting's key, the scope (SETTING_SCOPE_TENANT, _BRAND, _STORE_GROUP or _STORE), the id it is for, the value, and notice_confirmed (default false), true when the person confirmed the notice of a value its catalogue entry's confirm names

200.description: Written, and every store it reaches republished. The body lists each store with SETTING_PUBLISH_APPLIED and the new config version, SETTING_PUBLISH_UNCHANGED, or SETTING_PUBLISH_FAILED

400.description: An id is not a ULID, the scope is not a scope, the setting is not in the register, the setting cannot be set at that scope, the value is not one it takes, the value needs its notice confirmed and notice_confirmed is not true, or a tenant-scope value names another tenant

404.description: The tenant has no such brand, store group or store

409.description: The store group is archived, so its values reach no store

503.description: The settings store, the registry, the store groups or the config tree is unreachable

`DELETE /admin/settings` — clears one value and republishes every store it reached, which then
run the next most specific value, or the default.

parameters.name: scope_id
parameters.description: The tenant, brand, store group or store the value was written for

200.description: Cleared, and every store it reached republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a write

post.summary:
`POST /admin/settings/presets` — gives a store the values the owner chose for a new store
(ADR-0160 decision 1), which the console calls when it creates one.
post.description:
Only settings the store does not set itself are written, so calling it twice, or on a store an
operator has already configured, changes nothing the operator chose.

requestBody.description: The tenant and the store to give the new-store values

200.description: Each setting with a new-store value that the store did not already set is written at the store's own scope, and the store republished. The body lists the settings written and the store's publish outcome

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The settings store, the registry, the store groups or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary:
`POST /admin/settings/publish` — republishes the settings of one store, or of every store of the
tenant.
post.description:
A write republishes every store it reaches by itself. What it cannot see is a store that moved:
a store given another brand, or added to or removed from a store group, keeps the values it was
last published until this runs for it, as a group's batch publish works
([ADR-0122](../../../docs/adr/0122-a-store-group-is-a-delivery-cohort.md)).

requestBody.description: The tenant, and optionally one store. Without a store, every store of the tenant is republished

200.description: Each store's resolved settings republished, with the same per-store outcomes as a write

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The settings store, the registry, the store groups or the config tree is unreachable

post.summary: First-boot super-admin enrolment.
post.description:
[ADR-0045](../../../docs/adr/0045-first-boot-admin-enrolment.md).

Token-gated and self-disabling: `404` when no setup token is configured, `401` on a token mismatch
(compared in constant time), `400` if the chosen password is shorter than [`MIN_PASSWORD_LEN`],
`409` once an administrator is already enrolled, and on success `201` with the one-time TOTP
enrolment. The password is hashed with Argon2id under a fresh CSPRNG salt and never stored in the
clear; the TOTP secret is generated here and returned exactly once.

requestBody.description: The enrolment token from the server's environment, and the first administrator's chosen email and password

201.description: Enrolled. The body carries the one-time TOTP enrolment (QR payload and base32 secret) — returned exactly once, never readable again

400.description: The password is shorter than the minimum

409.description: An administrator is already enrolled

post.x-public-reason: the enrolment token from the server's environment, used once

parameters.description: The tenant whose cohorts to list (a 26-character ULID)

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: A super-admin creates an empty store group.
post.description:
Empty, deliberately: a group that started holding every store would make *creating* one an act
with a fleet-wide blast radius, and an operator naming a cohort has not yet said what is in it.

201.description: The group, with the ETag to hand back on its first edit. It holds no stores yet — membership is a second call, so naming a cohort is never itself an act with a fleet-wide reach

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or name is empty

503.description: The store-group store is unreachable, or OS entropy is unavailable to mint an id

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the group was read at (ADR-0094). Required

400.description: group_id or tenant_id is not a ULID, name is empty, or status is not active/archived
