parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The cohort whose history to read (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many batches, newest first (default 20, max 200)

200.description: The group's batches, newest first, each with its per-store outcomes. A member whose last batch was not `applied` is a store that is not running what its group runs

400.description: An id is not a ULID, or limit is out of range

get.summary: A super-admin reads one batch and what it did at every member.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The cohort the batch ran against (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The batch and an outcome for every member it reached

400.description: An id is not a ULID

404.description: No such batch on this group in this tenant

put.summary: A super-admin replaces a group's membership.
put.description:
Every id is checked against the tenant's own stores before anything is written. An id that names
no store of this tenant is a `422` rather than a stored row, because the failure it otherwise
produces is invisible: the cohort looks right on screen, and every batch quietly reports one more
`skipped` store than the operator expects, forever.

A group an assignment names changes who works at each store that joins or leaves it, so each
such store that is open is published its `permissions` node once the membership is saved
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 7), and the answer's `stores` says how each went. The membership before the write, and
whether an assignment names the group, are read first, so a failed read refuses a write that has
not happened.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The group whose membership to replace (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the group was read at (ADR-0094/0095 shape C). Required

200.description: The membership as stored, deduplicated, with the group's new ETag, and `stores`: when an assignment names the group, how the `permissions` publish went at each open store that joined or left it (ADR-0158), and empty otherwise

400.description: group_id, tenant_id or a store id is not a ULID

404.description: No such group in this tenant

412.description: If-Match is absent, or names a version the group has moved past

422.description: More than 200 stores, or an id that names no store of this tenant

503.description: The store-group store, the registry or the people store is unreachable

post.summary: A super-admin publishes one node to every member of a store group.
post.description:
The fan-out, in order: settle the instruction (which node, and can it compile at all), record
the batch, walk the membership recording an outcome for each, close the batch, answer with the
whole report. Nothing is written to any store until the instruction has compiled once, so an
unpublishable request costs no partial write; after that the batch does not stop, because
stopping is what turns one bad shop into fifty un-updated ones (ADR-0122 §5).

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The cohort to publish to (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The batch ran and every member has an outcome — `applied`, `skipped` or `failed`. A `200` does **not** mean every store succeeded: a batch is deliberately not atomic (ADR-0122 §5), and the per-store report is the answer

400.description: An id is not a ULID, the node is not one of the thirteen batchable kinds, or its arguments are the wrong shape

404.description: No such group in this tenant

422.description: The group is archived or empty, or the instruction itself is unpublishable (a menu that will not compile, an empty reason-code list) — nothing was written to any store

503.description: The store-group, registry or config store is unreachable

Behind [`ConsolePermission::Read`], the same gate the fleet view uses: "when did this store last
back up" is an operational fact every console role should be able to see, and a Viewer who
cannot see that a shop has not archived in a fortnight is a Viewer who cannot raise it.

requestBody.description: The tenant, the two country codes the console showed, and one sentence saying why the difference between them is correct

200.description: Recorded in the audit trail. The body is the answer as recorded

named version is unknown.

parameters.description: The configuration version the rollback was decided against (ADR-0095). Required

request body, and publishes — composing, validating, and (only if valid) appending a new version,
which is then persisted. A rejected version is a `422` carrying the violations; nothing is stored
and the last good version stays current ([ADR-0033](../../../docs/adr/0033-config-tree.md)).

get.summary:
Which devices a store has admitted, which it has retired, and when
([ADR-0118](../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §4).
get.description:
The read that makes `device.admission.granted` and `device.admission.revoked` a feature rather
than two events with no reader — the state the tree already had one of, and which that record
named as the thing not to repeat. Before this the console's picture of a store's tills was zero
rows, however many tablets the store had actually paired.

**T3**, so `console.data.read` — the same standing the fleet detail beside it takes. The roster
carries device identifiers and instants: no money, and **no employee**, because who admitted a
device is recorded on the store's own disk and reaches no cloud (ADR-0118 §5). The tenant is
named explicitly, as on every `/admin` read, because the console admin is global.

Unwindowed and unpaged: a store's roster is a handful of rows, at the rate it commissions tills.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store whose roster to read (a 26-character ULID)

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that store belongs to (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The store's admitted devices, still-admitted first and newest admission first within each group. Each entry carries the edge-minted local device id, when it was admitted, the paired device whose signed-in manager minted the code (absent for the code a box announces at boot), and when it was retired if it has been. A retired device keeps its row. Empty for a store that has admitted nothing, and for one whose rollup has not been projected yet

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary:
Retires one till on a store the console cannot otherwise reach
([ADR-0118](../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §6).
post.description:
**Appends to the `revoked_devices` node, never replaces it**, and the append happens *inside* the
conditional-write retry (see [`publish_config_nodes_with`]). Two admins each retiring a different
till therefore cannot lose each other's entry — which for a deny-list would mean a device left
trading that somebody was told had been retired.

**There is no un-revoke route, and that is the design.** The list is monotone: retiring a device
deletes its pairing row on the box, and no document can put it back. A till that legitimately
returns is a *fresh pairing* with a fresh id, which the list never names.

**A `200` is not proof the device is off.** It means the instruction is published. The store
applies it on its next pull and may refuse it whole — its blast-radius caps are the only place
the roster is authoritative — and it has no channel to say so. Read the admitted-devices roster
to see the retirement land; if it does not, the box's own log says why (ADR-0117).

`console.stores.manage` (Owner/Admin) rather than the `PublishConfig` norm that includes Ops. The
same standing as the lease bump beside it on the Fleet screen, and for the same reason: this is
not a day-to-day publish, it takes a terminal out of service, and a mistake can leave a shop
unable to sell.

The trail records the store and the device id. No employee: who at the console did this is the
audit row's actor, and no *store* employee is involved at all (ADR-0118 §5).

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store the till belongs to (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The deny-list now names the device, as of the config version returned. The store carries it out on its next config pull — within thirty seconds for a store with a working link, and on its next boot otherwise — and the admitted-devices roster then shows the device retired. Re-revoking a device already on the list succeeds and adds nothing

400.description: tenant_id, store_id or local_device_id is absent or not a ULID, or this store's deny-list is already at its cap

409.description: Concurrent config publishes kept winning the race

422.description: The composed node did not validate

200.description: Updated. The body is the record and the ETag carries its new version. Audited

400.description: An id is not a ULID, status is not `active` or `archived`, or If-Match is absent, malformed, or a wildcard

404.description: The store has no device slot with that id

412.description: The slot changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

get.summary:
`GET /admin/stores/{store_id}/permissions/readiness` — what each role held at a store does not
grant, read before the store enforces each person's own permissions.
get.description:
The roles are those the store's `permissions` node is compiled from: every assignment that
reaches the store, whatever its scope, held by an active person, with an active role. Each is
compared with the permission catalogue and nothing else; what anybody did at the till is not
read (ADR-0070).

200.description: `store_id`; `enforced`, what the store runs for `permissions.enforced`, with `enforced_scope` and `enforced_scope_id` naming the value's level, both absent for the default; `roles`, one per active role an active person holds at the store through any assignment that reaches it, by name, each with `role_template_id`, `name`, `people` (how many hold it, each once) and `missing` — every permission a store decides that the role grants neither directly nor with approval, as `id`, `group` and `risk`, low risk first and catalogue order within a level; and `people_without_role`, how many people at the store hold no active role there. No person is named

400.description: store_id or tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no such store

503.description: The people store, the settings store, the registry or the store groups is unreachable

post.summary:
An admin records why a store's region difference is correct
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).
post.description:
Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageStores`] rather than `PublishConfig`: this is a judgement about
where a store's data may rest, which is the same judgement the bump that put it there was, and
the person who makes it is the person who moves stores between machines.

# It answers one difference, not the store

The request names both country codes and the write refuses `FailedPrecondition` when either has
moved since the console drew the screen. Without that check an admin could acknowledge a
difference that no longer exists — or worse, one that changed to something they never saw — and
the record would say a person approved a transfer they were never shown. The row then keeps the
pair, so the *read* applies the same rule for free: an answer stops standing when the store
moves, and the warning comes back unanswered.

Refused for a store with no difference at all, because there is nothing to answer: a store whose
region agrees, or which has no region, or which has published no country, would otherwise
accumulate reasons for questions nobody asked.

requestBody.description: The tenant, the two country codes the console showed, and one sentence saying why the difference between them is correct

200.description: Recorded. The body is the answer as stored

400.description: A country code is not two letters, or the reason is blank or over 280 characters

404.description: The tenant has no such store

409.description: Nothing to answer, or the store has moved since this screen was drawn — the codes you named are not the ones it has now

503.description: The fleet, the config tree, or the acknowledgement store is unreachable

Windowed as the revenue read is, and long-format: a file of its own rather than columns added to

so it needs `console.reports.revenue`, as `GET /admin/stores/{store_id}/revenue/export` does,

A file of its own beside `revenue-fees.csv`, and the same in every way that matters: windowed
as the revenue read is, behind `console.reports.revenue`, and audited by how many rows were
exported, never what they held.

The header is `business_date,currency_code,component_name,rate_basis_points,tax`, then one row per trading day per tax component name and rate the day's settled bills recorded, oldest day first and then by name and rate: the tax their tax lines recorded under it, in the store's currency's minor units. [ADR-0067](../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md) slice 6. Re-confirms the current
password (the knowledge factor) before rotating the TOTP secret (the possession factor), so a
session-only attacker — one holding the cookie but not the password — cannot lock the owner out by
re-enrolling. On success the new one-time enrolment (QR + base32 secret) is returned once; existing
sessions stay valid, and the next sign-in uses the new authenticator.

requestBody.description: The acting administrator's current password — re-asked so a session-only attacker cannot rotate the second factor and lock the owner out

200.description: Re-enrolled. The new one-time enrolment (QR payload and base32 secret) is returned once; existing sessions stay valid and the next sign-in uses the new authenticator

401.description: No live session, or the password is wrong

get.summary: Returns a tenant's translation grid (super-admin only), or an empty grid if it has authored none.

200.description: The tenant's grid: each content key to its strings by locale, every key carrying `en`, the fallback. The grid is one entity: its version is the response's ETag. A tenant with no grid yet gets an empty one and no ETag

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

put.summary:
Replaces a tenant's translation grid (super-admin only). A grid whose every key does not carry a
non-empty `en` is a `422` naming the offending keys, and nothing is stored.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the grid was read at, or `*` for a tenant with no grid yet (ADR-0095)

requestBody.description: The whole grid, as the read returns it: each content key to its strings by locale. It replaces the stored grid

204.description: Replaced, and audited. The ETag carries the new version

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or If-Match is absent or malformed

404.description: If-Match named a version, but the tenant has no grid yet

412.description: The grid changed since you read it: re-read it and try again

422.description: A key has no non-empty `en` string, naming each such key. Nothing is stored

get.summary:
A super-admin exports a tenant's translation grid as CSV ([ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md),
Track M5). Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageTranslations`] and audited (who exported which domain
and how many rows, never the row contents). The grid is business copy (menu/UI strings), not
personal data.

200.description: `translations.csv`, as a `text/csv` attachment: a `key` column, then one column per locale present, sorted, and a row per content key. A cell a spreadsheet would read as a formula is escaped. Audited by row count, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

500.description: The CSV could not be built

post.summary:
A super-admin applies a translation-grid CSV import ([ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md),
Track M5) — the confirm after a dry-run. The valid rows are merged onto the tenant's grid (existing
keys not in the file are preserved; rejected rows are skipped) and saved; rejected rows are reported,
never written. Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageTranslations`] and audited (the row counts, never
the contents). The merged grid still satisfies the `en`-fallback rule by construction.

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/translations/export` writes, as the raw request body: a `key` column, then one column per locale, at most 4 MB. Rows are merged onto the grid: the keys in the file are set and every other key is kept

200.description: Applied: the valid rows are merged onto the grid and saved, and the report is `rows`, one per data row with its `key` and its `action` (`create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`), and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. A merge needs no If-Match: the server re-reads and retries when another writer got there first. The ETag carries the grid's new version. Audited by counts, never the contents

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or the body is not CSV of the export's shape

412.description: Every attempt lost a race with another writer: try again

413.description: The body is over 4 MB. Answered by the server's body limit, without the error envelope

post.summary:
A super-admin dry-runs a translation-grid CSV import ([ADR-0075](../../../docs/adr/0075-media-and-file-rail.md),
Track M5): the server parses and classifies every row (would-create / would-update / rejected) and
returns the report, **writing nothing**. Behind [`ConsolePermission::ManageTranslations`]; not
audited (it changes nothing). The confirm step (`.../apply`) does the write.

requestBody.description: The CSV `GET /admin/translations/export` writes, as the raw request body: a `key` column, then one column per locale, at most 4 MB. Rows are merged onto the grid: the keys in the file are set and every other key is kept

200.description: What the file would do, writing nothing: `rows`, one per data row with its `key` and its `action` (`create`, `update`, or `reject` with a `reason`), and `create_count`, `update_count` and `reject_count`. A row with no `en` string is rejected. Not audited

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID, or the body is not CSV of the export's shape

413.description: The body is over 4 MB. Answered by the server's body limit, without the error envelope

get.summary: Lists a tenant's webhook endpoints as metadata only — never a secret (super-admin only).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant whose endpoints to list (a 26-character ULID)

200.description: The tenant's endpoints, as an array: each with `id`, `store_id`, `url`, `cursor` (the last event delivered, absent before the first) and `disabled`. Never the signing secret

400.description: tenant_id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary: Registers a webhook endpoint and returns the one-time signing secret (super-admin only).
post.description:
Behind the session guard. The destination is SSRF-vetted before anything is stored: `https` only,
no credentials, and every resolved address must be public unicast — so a webhook URL can never
become a probe into the cloud's own network ([ADR-0032](../../../docs/adr/0032-webhooks.md)). The
id and signing secret are minted at the edge; the secret in the `201` body is the only time it is
visible, because the cloud stores it to *sign* with rather than to verify a hash of.

requestBody.description: `tenant_id`, `store_id`, the store whose events the endpoint is sent, and `url`: `https`, carrying no credentials, and resolving only to public addresses (ADR-0032). The URL is checked before anything is stored

201.description: Registered. The body carries the endpoint's `id`, the normalised `url` that was stored, and the `signing_secret` every delivery is signed with. The secret is returned exactly once

400.description: tenant_id or store_id is not a ULID, or the URL is refused. The refusal names the `url` field and does not say what this server's resolver found

503.description: The endpoint store, the URL check or the entropy source is unavailable

delete.summary:
Deletes a webhook endpoint by id within a tenant (super-admin only). `204` whether or not a live
endpoint was found — deletion is idempotent, the tenant scope stops one tenant removing another's
endpoint, and reporting which case it was is a needless enumeration signal.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

204.description: The tenant has no endpoint with that id any more. Idempotent: the answer is the same whether one was found, and another tenant's endpoint is never removed

400.description: tenant_id or id is absent or not a ULID

post.summary:
Re-enables a webhook endpoint that a day of continuous failure had auto-disabled (super-admin
only). Delivery resumes from the endpoint's stored cursor, so nothing that queued while it was
down is skipped ([ADR-0032](../../../docs/adr/0032-webhooks.md)).
post.description:
Tenant-scoped like deletion, but enforced differently: [`WebhookEndpointStore::set_disabled`]
addresses an endpoint by id alone — the delivery task, which also calls it, holds no tenant — so
the scope is checked here by confirming the id appears in this tenant's own listing before the
flag is cleared. An id that is not this tenant's is a `404`, never a cross-tenant write. Idempotent:
re-enabling an already-active endpoint is a no-op `204`.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The tenant that owns it (a 26-character ULID)

204.description: Enabled. Delivery resumes from the endpoint's stored cursor, so nothing queued while it was disabled is skipped. Enabling an endpoint already enabled changes nothing

400.description: tenant_id or id is absent or not a ULID

404.description: The tenant has no endpoint with that id

get.summary: The acting admin's own identity — id, email, name, role, status.
get.description:
So a console can label the signed-in operator and show only the areas their role grants
([ADR-0067](../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md) slice 7). Self-service: available
to any authenticated admin regardless of role, so it is gated by the plain session guard rather
than a [`ConsolePermission`]. It returns the same credential-free [`AdminUser`] shape the roster
lists — never a password hash or a TOTP secret — and role gating in the console is only a UX
convenience; the server re-checks every route's required permission regardless.

200.description: The acting administrator — id, email, role, status — never a password hash or a TOTP secret. Role gating in a console is a convenience only: the server re-checks every route's required permission regardless

AcceptInviteRequest.description:
A self-enrolment request: the single-use invite token and the password the invitee chooses.

[`fmt::Debug`] redacts both, so a logged request cannot leak the token or the password.

password.description: The password the invitee is choosing.

token.description: The single-use invite token from the invite link.

AcknowledgeCellRequest.description:
What a console sends to answer a store's cell warning. The two countries say which difference is
answered: a write naming a pair the store no longer has is refused.

cell_country.description: The cell's country the console showed.

profile_country.description: The store's country the console showed.

reason.description:
Why the difference is correct: required, at most 280 characters. Defaulted so an omitted
field is refused through the envelope naming it.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the store belongs to.

AcknowledgeRegionRequest.description:
What a console sends to answer a store's region warning
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

**The two country codes are the precondition, and they are in the body rather than in an
`If-Match` header.** ADR-0114's Consequences said `If-Match`; the code does not, and the reason
is the one [`LeaseStore::settle_handover`] already gives one table over: *the named value is the
precondition*, and here it is strictly stronger than any version could be. There is no single
resource whose `ETag` covers both halves of this comparison — the region lives on `store_lease`
and the country lives in the config tree, two rows with two independent writers — so an
`If-Match` would have to name one of them and silently miss changes to the other. Naming both
codes catches every move of either, and says in the request exactly what the admin was looking at
when they decided. The departure is written up in the record's delivery note.

profile_country.description: The country the console showed as the store's own when the admin decided.

reason.description:
Why the difference is correct. Required, non-blank, at most [`REGION_REASON_LIMIT`]
characters. `#[serde(default)]` so an omitted field is refused through the AIP-193 envelope
naming it, rather than by axum's extractor as a bare `422`.

region_country.description: The country the console showed the store's data resting in when the admin decided.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the store belongs to.

AdminInvite.description:
A pending or accepted invitation, as listed ([ADR-0067](../../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md)).
Carries no token — only its `SHA-256` is ever stored — so this is safe to serialise to the console.

accepted.description: Whether the invite has been accepted (its self-enrolment completed).

email.description: The address the invitee will sign in with once they accept.

id.description: The invite's ULID id.

invited_by.description: The id of the admin who issued the invite.

name.description: The display name the accepted admin will carry.

role.description: The role the accepted admin will be granted.

AdminRole.description:
A console admin's role — the least-privilege tier its session is granted
([ADR-0067](../../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md)). This is the stable vocabulary the
schema and seam store; the role→permission templates (the compile-forced §9-style registry) land
in a later G1 slice and are built on top of these variants.

AdminSessionView.description:
One of the acting admin's live sessions, as the console lists it. `id` is the opaque revocation
handle (hex of `SHA-256(token)` — never the token, and not reversible to it); `current` marks the
session making this very request, which the console protects from accidental self-revocation.

created_at_ms.description: When the session was minted (Unix ms).

current.description: Whether this is the session making the current request.

expires_at_ms.description: When the session currently expires (Unix ms), after any sliding.

id.description: The opaque handle the console revokes this session by.

ip.description: The client IP the session was minted for, if it was known.

user_agent.description: The client user-agent the session was minted for, if it was known.

AdminStatus.description:
Whether an admin can sign in. `Suspended` keeps the row and its history but refuses new sessions —
the off-boarding path that does not destroy the audit trail.

AdminUser.description:
A console admin as listed — identity and role, never the credential. Safe to serialise to the
console: it carries no password hash and no TOTP secret.

email.description: The login identity. Unique case-insensitively across admins.

id.description: The admin's ULID id (a string; minted at the HTTP edge).

role.description: The role that decides the session's permissions.

status.description: Whether the admin can sign in.

AdmittedDevice.description:
One device a store has admitted, as the fleet console finally sees it
([ADR-0118](../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §4).

Folded from `device.admission.granted` and `device.admission.revoked`. Until those events the
cloud's picture of a store's tills was **zero rows**, so a lost tablet meant sending somebody to
the store and a remote revocation had nothing to name.

# Not the console's named-device registry, and not confusable with it

`local_device_id` is minted by the **edge** at redemption (ADR-0030); the `devices` table's ids
are minted by the **console** when an admin names a terminal. Nothing joins the two, by decision
— a browser till presents no identity of its own and clearing its storage creates a new device —
so this roster sits beside that registry rather than inside it. A row here means *this store
admitted this thing*, which is the fact the registry has never been able to state.

**T3 (internal): device identifiers and instants, no money and no person.** Who admitted a
device is deliberately absent — that is recorded on the store's own disk and reaches no cloud
(ADR-0118 §5). `admitted_by_device_id` is a *device*, the till whose signed-in manager minted the
code.

admitted_at_ms.description: When it was admitted, Unix ms — the event's own instant, so a re-projection reproduces it.

admitted_by_device_id.description:
The paired till whose signed-in manager minted the code, where one did. `None` for the code a
box announces at boot, which nothing authorised because nothing could.

local_device_id.description: The edge-minted device id the store issued a token to.

revoked_at_ms.description:
When the store retired it, Unix ms, or `None` while it is still admitted. A revocation does
not delete the row: a roster that forgets what it retired cannot answer "was this tablet ever
here", which is the first question asked about a device that turns up somewhere it should not.

AlertView.description:
The console's view of a stored alert: the record with the kind/severity as their wire tokens and
the lifecycle instants as Unix ms.

ApiKeySummary.description:
A key's metadata for a listing — everything but the secret and its hash, which never leave the
store. Serialises to the `/admin/api-keys` list response.

expires_at_ms.description: When the key expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, if ever.

id.description: The public id (the ULID half of the token).

revoked.description: Whether the key has been revoked.

scopes.description: The granted scopes, as their wire names, sorted.

store_id.description: The store this key is bound to, or `None` for a tenant-wide key (S1).

ArchiveView.description:
One archive as the console sees it.

No key and nothing that could open one — this is the *index*, and the key is a separate,
deliberate ask. `object_key` is here because it is what an operator types into a restore.

object_key.description: Where the bytes are in the object store.

received_at_ms.description:
When the cloud received it, Unix ms. The gap between the two is how far behind a store's
uplink was.

sha256.description:
The cloud's hex SHA-256 of the sealed bytes as they arrived, so a download can be checked
before anybody spends time on a key.

taken_at_ms.description:
When the store took the snapshot, Unix ms. **This is the recovery point** — not
`received_at_ms`, which is when a possibly-delayed upload landed.

Area.description: An area as the console reads it: a named region of one store's floor.

store_id.description: The store this area belongs to.

AreaId.description: A `AreaId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ArtifactFetchOutcome.description:
What a fetch did with one artifact: `recorded` for a new one, `already_hosted` for one the cloud
already held with these exact bytes, so a re-run reads as a no-op rather than as work.

ArtifactUploaded.description: What an artifact upload answers: the artifact it recorded.

allOf.description: Where it grants the role: `scope_kind`, and `store_id` or `store_group_id` beside it.

employee_code.description: The assigned person's staff code, `None` on the same terms as the name.

employee_name.description: The assigned person's name, or `None` if no employee row matches `employee_id`.

role_template_id.description: The role it grants wherever it reaches.

Assignment.description:
A person's assignment with a role, at one store, a store group or every store of the tenant
([`AssignmentScope`]). Every id is the same tenant (the `tenant_id` column + RLS isolate them;
the route layer checks referential validity before writing).

# Who the assignment is for

The row carries the assigned person's name and code alongside their id, resolved by the store as
it reads. Without them a caller can only name the person by looking the id up in the tenant's
roster, which is a whole-set read the console cannot keep making once the roster is paged
([ADR-0098](../../../docs/adr/0098-paged-admin-reads.md), B3-4).

Both are `Option`, and the reason is in the schema rather than the domain: nothing declares a
foreign key from an assignment to an employee, so an assignment can outlive the row it names.
`None` means exactly that, and a caller should fall back to showing the id — the assignment is
real and still grants access, so hiding it would be worse than showing it unlabelled.

The name and code are T1 personal data
([ADR-0070](../../../docs/adr/0070-people-and-access.md)) and reaching them needs
`console.people.read`, the same gate as reading the roster
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)).

AssignmentCreated.description:
What an assignment's create answers: the id it minted, and, where the assignment reached a
store at once, how publishing to each went (ADR-0158 decision 7).

id.description: The new assignment's id, a ULID.

stores.description: One result per store the assignment reached, absent when it reached none.

AssignmentId.description: An assignment's identifier — a ULID minted at creation.

store_id.description: The one store it reaches, a ULID

store_group_id.description: The group whose stores it reaches when read, a ULID

AssignmentScope.description: Where an assignment grants its role: `scope_kind`, with `store_id` for one store, `store_group_id` for a group, and neither for every store of the tenant

AuditEntryView.description:
One audit entry as the console reads it: ids as strings (the screen shows names/labels, not raw
ULIDs front-and-centre), the actor snapshot flattened, and the instant as Unix ms.

allOf.description: The rule's own fields, as the wire carries them.

item_category_ids.description: The item categories it names, absent when it names none.

AuthoredFeeRule.description:
A fee rule as its author wrote it: the wire rule's fields, and the item categories it names,
which the store is sent compiled into items. The same bytes as the rule store keeps
([`crate::fees::authored_json`]), which `authored_rule_tests` holds.

oneOf.description: A flag.
A whole number.
Text, a URL, or one of a fixed set of choices.

additionalProperties.description:
A non-secret setting's value, as the operator typed it: the plain JSON its schema's kind implies.

Untagged, so `true`, `30` and `"192.0.2.40"` are the values themselves. Whole numbers only — a
setting is an address, a port, a count or a timeout, never an amount, and money is never a
float anywhere in this workspace.

BatchOutcome.description:
What a batch publish did at one store.

Three variants, because there are three real answers to "what happened at this shop", and the
distinction between the first two is the whole reason the report exists.

BatchReport.description: A batch and what it did at every member — the response body, and the read routes' shape.

finished_at_ms.description: Absent for a batch that died mid-fan-out — exactly the row an operator goes looking for.

BatchResultView.description: What a batch did at one store.

config_version_id.description: The config version the publish produced, for `applied`.

detail.description:
The refusal's own message, for `skipped` and `failed`. For `applied`, absent unless the
write left something behind: a menu whose store's fees did not go with it says so, with the
fee publish's outcome and reason tokens.

outcome.description: `applied`, `skipped` or `failed`: exactly the three of ADR-0122 §6.

BindClaimRequest.description: A console user binds the code a box shows to a device slot.

BrandId.description:
A brand's public identifier — a ULID minted at creation. The other three entities already have id
types in [`pos_proto::ids`]; a brand is new here, so its id is defined alongside the seam.

BrandRecord.description: A brand — grouped under a tenant.

BumpLeaseRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/lease/bump` body: the `(tenant, store)` whose next generation to issue, and
optionally where the machine taking it runs
([ADR-0110](../../../docs/adr/0110-edge-placement-is-a-deployment-axis.md)).

`edge_placement` absent means "replace the machine where the store already is" — ADR-0003's swap,
and every bump this route served before the field existed, which is why it defaults rather than
being required. Present, it means the store is **moving**, and this is the only route in the tree
that writes the value.

acknowledge_undrained.description:
The undrained generation this bump is knowingly abandoning, or absent.

It names the value already sitting in `superseded_generation` — *not* the generation this
bump is about to displace. So an acknowledged bump does not clear the column; it rolls it
forward, and the fact that the older generation was abandoned survives in the audit trail,
which is why the entry carries both numbers.

region_country.description:
Where in the world the machine taking this generation is — its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

Required together with `region_label` when `edge_placement` names a hosted mode, and refused
on any other bump: an in-store machine is in the shop, and a bump that names no placement is
a swap in place, so a region on either would be a region edited without moving the store.

region_label.description:
The place a person recognises — `ap-southeast-1`, `Ho Chi Minh City`, `the rack in Sakai`.

Stored verbatim and never parsed by anything. It is free text an admin typed, so the
console's helper text asks for a place and not a person; it is never logged and never enters
an event payload.

CampaignId.description: A `CampaignId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

CampaignRequest.description:
A create/update body: the tenant and the campaign's authoring fields. The id is **server-owned** —
minted on create, the path id on update — so a client never supplies or forges it. Everything else
is the wire campaign's own shape (kind, action, conditions), reused rather than re-declared.

CampaignsScheduled.description: What scheduling a campaign publish answers: the scheduled publish and when it takes effect.

effective_at_ms.description: When it publishes, in Unix milliseconds.

id.description: The scheduled publish's id, a ULID.

CapabilityCatalogueView.description:
The whole capability catalogue the form editor needs: the flags, the presets, and the inter-flag
rules — all §10 data, tenant-independent.

CapabilityFlagView.description:
One capability flag as the console's form editor reads it: its config key, default, and the
one-line description (§10 catalogue). Mirrors `pos-core`'s `CapabilityMeta` so the console renders
toggles from the framework's own source of truth rather than a hand-kept list.

offered.description:
Whether the console offers the flag as a switch: `false` for one no release reads yet
([`offered`]).

CapabilityPresetView.description:
One capability preset (§10) — a named starting profile the console offers as a button, given as the
set of flag keys it turns on.

CapabilityRuleView.description:
One inter-flag rule (§10) the console previews before publish, so a conflict shows the moment it is
created rather than as a `422` on publish.

CashTotals.description:
A day's cash figures for one drawer (part of [`DailyCash`]), the same as the store's.

The store's stay inline on [`DailyCash`] rather than in one of these under
`#[serde(flatten)]`, which would keep the wire as it is and does not pass the lints: the
flatten buffer carries `f32` and `f64`, which `clippy.toml` bans (money is never a float).

counted.description: Sum of counted amounts across closes (the blind counts).

expected.description:
Sum of expected drawer amounts across closes. Only a close carries one: the edge works out
what a drawer should hold at its close, so a shift still open adds nothing here.

opening_float.description: Sum of opening floats across shifts opened on the day.

variance.description: Sum of variance (counted − expected) across closes; negative is short.

CatalogDisplayCategory.description:
A display category — the **presentation** taxonomy a screen groups by (ADR-0066 entity 11).

Deliberately distinct from an [`ItemCategory`] (the operational taxonomy): a screen may show a
"Summer specials" tab whose items report under "Pizza". Its id is a [`DisplayCategoryId`] — the
same id the compiled [`pos_proto::DisplayCategory`] carries, the way an item's id crosses into the
compiled `MenuEntry`.

display_category_id.description: The display-category id — carried into the compiled `DisplayPlan`.

name.description: The name a screen shows as a tab or section.

CatalogDisplaySubcategory.description: A display sub-category — a second grouping level under a [`DisplayCategory`] (ADR-0066 entity 11).

display_subcategory_id.description: The display-sub-category id — carried into the compiled plan.

CatalogItem.description:
An item in the catalog — the product master.

Its id is a [`MenuItemId`], the same identifier the compiled [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`] names and an
inbound order references: the item authored here is the item priced downstream. This slice carries
the fields a `MenuEntry` needs (name, tax class); its operational category, recipe/BOM link and
the rest arrive with later slices.

oneOf.description:
The course this item goes out on, or `None` for an item on no course
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md) decision 3).

Carried on the item exactly as [`tax_class_id`](Self::tax_class_id) is, and for the same
reason: a pizza is a main, and making a server say so on every tap would be a tap per dish
for a fact the catalog already knows. `None` is every item in every store today and stays
correct.

A **per-line override** is deliberately not modelled. The request it would serve — *"bring my
main with the starters"* — is about when the food goes, and firing already answers that;
relabelling a line's course to mean "sooner" would put a timing decision inside a taxonomy.

The item's photo — a [`MediaId`] into the media library (ADR-0075), or `None`. Authoring/display
only; it does not cross to the edge. A dangling ref (the asset was deleted) shows a placeholder.
The operational category this item reports under, or `None` if unclassified (entity 2).
The operational sub-category, refining the category, or `None` (entity 3).

menu_item_id.description: The item's id — shared with the compiled menu entry and any inbound order that names it.

name.description:
The human name (the default caption, before a layout overrides it per channel). Always
present, and the fallback for a locale [`name_translations`](Self::name_translations) omits.

name_translations.description:
The item's name in each locale it is translated into, keyed by locale code (`"vi"`, `"en"`, …)
([ADR-0074](../../../docs/adr/0074-localization-and-tax.md), Track M4). The compiler carries
these onto the [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`]; the store's display language selects one at the edge,
falling back to [`name`](Self::name). Additive — an item with none behaves as before.

tax_class_id.description: The tax class, which the store's channel-keyed rate table turns into a rate at reprice time.

CatalogueConfirm.description:
A catalogue entry's `confirm`: the value that needs confirming, and the translation key of the
notice the Settings screen shows beside it.

CatalogueView.description: The catalogue as the console reads it.

providers.description: Every provider, grouped by family in [`Family::ALL`]'s order and in listed order within one.

CellAcknowledgementView.description: A recorded answer to a store's cell difference.

acknowledged_at_ms.description: When it was recorded, in milliseconds since the epoch.

cell_country.description: The cell's country the answer was about.

profile_country.description: The store's country the answer was about.

reason.description: Why the difference is correct, as typed.

CellDirectoryMode.description: Which kind of answer the cell gives about where a tenant is (ADR-0179 C2).

CellStandingView.description: A store's country against its cell's.

oneOf.description: The answer to this difference, while it is still this difference.

cell_country.description:
The cell's home country. Null when the cell has no `[cell]` section, which compares with
nothing.

cell_id.description: The cell this store's data rests in.

differs.description: Whether both are known and differ. A warning, never a refusal.

profile_country.description: The country the store publishes in its `locale` node. Null when it has published none.

CellView.description:
This cell as the console reads it: the `[cell]` section, fixed when the server starts, and the
directory it answers from now. The same for every tenant. It holds no personal data and no
secret.

base_url.description: The origin this cell answers on. Null when no `[cell]` section is configured.

cell_id.description: The cell id (`vn1`), or `default` when `cloud.toml` has no `[cell]` section.

configured.description: Whether `cloud.toml` carries a `[cell]` section. False is level 0: the one and only cell.

country_alias.description: The country alias (`vn`), when one is configured.

directory_mode.description: Which kind of answer the cell gives about where a tenant is.

directory_refusal.description:
Why the last directory offered was refused, until one is accepted. The directory held, if
any, is kept.

directory_version.description: The version of the signed directory held. Null unless one is.

home_country.description:
The country this cell's tenants are homed by (`VN`). Null when no `[cell]` section is
configured.

runs_abroad.description:
Whether the servers run in a different country from the home country. A warning, never a
refusal.

runs_in.description: The country this cell's servers run in. Null when no `[cell]` section is configured.

ChainFindingView.description:
One refused chain claim on the wire.

Positions, hashes and identifiers — no event contents and no customer identifier. A chain hash is
a digest of an envelope whose every payload field `pos_proto::pii` has already proven free of
personal data.

chain_seq.description: The chain length both hashes claim to describe.

finding_id.description:
The finding's id, derived from the contradiction rather than minted, so a re-delivery of the
same bad claim does not multiply into rows.

noticed_at_ms.description:
Unix ms when the **cloud** noticed. The server's clock, which is the one an investigation can
rely on — the store's is on the anchor, and a store that is tampering controls that one.

offered_event_id.description: The event that carried the offered claim, so the finding traces back to a record.

offered_head.description: What it was offered against it.

store_id.description: The store whose log disagrees with itself (a ULID string).

ChannelPrice.description:
One channel's price for a [`MenuPlacement`].

This is where dine-in ≠ takeaway ≠ delivery pricing is authored; the compiler emits one channel's
prices into that channel's [`pos_proto::MenuCatalog`] within the store's `MenuBook`.

sales_channel.description:
The channel this price applies on. `Open`, the same shape [`pos_proto::locale::TaxRateRow`]
uses, so authoring stored under a channel a later build learns still round-trips.

unit_price.description: The price per unit on that channel. Integer [`Money`].

ConfigNodeView.description:
One node of a store's published configuration, as the console lists it (finding **F6**).

The console's question has always been per node — "is the menu this store is running the menu I
last edited?" — and until now the only answer available was per tree: one version id covering
thirteen nodes, so publishing a tax change made the menu look freshly published too. Every
version now records which nodes it wrote ([`PublishedVersion::nodes`]), and this is that read.

at_ms.description: When that version was published (from its ULID's own timestamp, Unix ms), or `null` with it.

node.description: The node key — `locale`, `tax`, `menu`, `permissions`, and so on.

version_id.description:
The version that last published this node, or `null` when no recorded version names it.

`null` is *not* "never published": the node is in the effective document, so it was. It means
the version that put it there predates this field, or was a whole-layer replace that named
nothing. The console says "published, when is not recorded" rather than inventing a date.

ConfigNodesView.description:
The per-node publish state of one store's configuration.

`current_version_id` is the tree's newest version, which is what a store *should* be holding. The
version it *is* holding is on the fleet read (`GET /admin/fleet/stores/{id}`), which every screen
that asks this question has already loaded — so it is not repeated here, and the comparison
happens where both numbers already are.

ConfigPreview.description:
What publishing a candidate node *would* change, computed without minting a version or saving:
the RFC 7386 merge patch from the store's current effective document to the candidate, so the
console can show a real before/after before anyone commits ([ADR-0077](../../../docs/adr/0077-campaigns-and-scheduling.md)).

diff.description:
The RFC 7386 merge patch a publish would apply to the effective document. An empty object
means the candidate composes to exactly today's effective document.

from_version_id.description:
The version the diff is computed against — the store's current version — or `null` when the
store has no published configuration yet (the candidate is then entirely new).

unchanged.description: True when `diff` is empty — nothing would change, so there is nothing to publish.

ConfigVersionView.description:
One published config version as the console lists it: the version id, when it was published (from
the ULID's own timestamp, Unix ms), and whether it is the store's current version.

ConnectionRequest.description:
A create/update body for a connection. The id is server-owned: minted on create, the path id on
update.

`secrets` holds only the values this write sets. A secret field left out keeps the value the
connection already holds, because the console cannot show it to be sent back. `clear_secrets`
removes a stored value on purpose. Switching `provider_id` drops every stored secret: one
vendor's key is never another's, even when both call the field `api_key`.

enabled.description: Absent means enabled: a caller that omits it is setting up a connection to use.

processing_country.description:
The country the vendor processes this connection's data in (`SG`), when known (ADR-0179
C7). Recorded, compared with the cell's home country, and never a reason to refuse.

ConnectionView.description: A connection as the API answers it: the record without its sealed values.

processing_country.description: The country the vendor processes this connection's data in, when recorded.

processing_outside_cell.description:
Whether that country is known and differs from the cell's home country. A warning, never a
refusal (ADR-0179 C7).

secrets_set.description: Which secret fields have a value. The values themselves are never returned.

CountryView.description:
One compiled country module as the console reads it: the code, human name, currency, preferred
language, number format, the default retention period, and the till facts its coinage and its
quoting habit fix. What the platform can serve — not a per-store setting, and not fiscalization.

The last three are what make a country **choosable** rather than merely listed
([ADR-0105](../../../docs/adr/0105-a-country-pack-is-values.md)): a store-settings form reads them
to fill its own fields in, so provisioning a Japanese shop does not depend on somebody remembering
that Japanese prices are tax-inclusive.

currency_exponent.description:
How many decimal places that currency has
([ADR-0134](../../../docs/adr/0134-a-currency-says-how-many-decimals-it-has.md)). Beside the
code because the console's own money fields edit minor units and need the same fact the till
does.

Course.description:
A course — the **service** taxonomy, when a dish goes out
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md)).

Deliberately distinct from an [`ItemCategory`] (operational — what an item reports under) and from
a [`DisplayCategory`] (presentational — where a screen puts it). A dessert wine reports under
drinks and goes out with dessert, and collapsing any two of the three would make one of those
facts unsayable.

The `sort` is the point rather than decoration: "starter before main before dessert" is the
entire meaning of the grouping, and a set of names with no order is a taxonomy rather than a
service sequence. Ties break by id in the compiler, as everywhere else, so a re-compile of
unchanged authoring stays byte-identical.

Its id is [`pos_proto::ids::CourseId`], which has crossed the seam since the schema was written —
it is on `sales.order_line.added` and on a published routing rule. The entity is what was
missing.

sort.description:
Where it falls in the service sequence, ascending. Not unique: two courses a store considers
interchangeable may share a position, and forcing an operator to renumber the whole menu to
insert one between two others would be a worse rule than letting the id break the tie.

status.description:
Active or archived. An archived course is not published, the same posture an archived item
and an archived modifier group already get.

CourseId.description: A `CourseId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: A super-admin request to provision a new API key for a tenant.

expires_at_ms.description: An optional expiry, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Omit for a key that never expires.

scopes.description: The scopes to grant, as their wire names (`read_rollups`, …). Deny-by-default: only these.

store_id.description:
The one store the key will act for (a ULID), or absent for a tenant-wide key.

A store's own credential — the key its edge presents on `/sync/stores/{store_id}/…` — must
name its store here: those routes serve one store's configuration, including its employee
roster and PIN hashes, and refuse a key that is not bound to the store in the path (S1). A
tenant-wide key stays right for an integration reading a whole tenant's rollups.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the key will act for (a 26-character ULID).

CreateApiKeyResponse.description: The one-time response to a provisioning request: the id, and the token shown exactly once.

id.description: The key's public id (the ULID half of the token).

token.description:
The full `pos_<id>_<secret>` token. **Shown once** — only its hash is stored, so it cannot be
recovered later.

CreateAssignmentRequest.description:
Assign an employee with a role, at one store, a store group or every store of the tenant
(ADR-0158 decision 3) — see [`requested_scope`] for how the three fields name one.

scope_kind.description:
An [`AssignmentScopeKind`] token. Absent, or `ASSIGNMENT_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED`, the scope is
the one the id sent names.

store_group_id.description: The group, for an assignment to every store it holds.

store_id.description: The store, for an assignment to one store.

CreateCourseRequest.description: Create a course — a named point in the service sequence (ADR-0130).

sort.description:
Where it falls in the sequence, ascending. Absent is `0`, which puts a first course first
and leaves the id to break the tie with any other unpositioned one.

CreateEmployeeRequest.description: Create an employee — identity only; the PIN is set separately.

course_id.description:
The course this item goes out on (ADR-0130). Absent leaves it on none, which is every item
in every store today.

image_ref.description: The item's photo — a media id (ADR-0075), or absent/empty for none.

name_translations.description:
Per-locale names keyed by locale code (ADR-0074). Optional and additive; `name` is the
always-present fallback.

CreateLayoutButtonRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/catalog/layout-buttons` body: a button's presentation plus the `(channel, item)`
slot it goes in, which the collection URI has no room for and the `PUT` takes from its path.

The identity fields are spelled out here rather than `#[serde(flatten)]`-ing the update body:
flatten pulls in serde's buffering `Content` enum, whose `f32`/`f64` variants `clippy.toml` bans
outright (`docs/adr/0013`: money is never a float). `into_write` keeps the two shapes from
drifting instead.

CreatePlacementRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/catalog/menus/{menu_id}/placements` body: a placement plus the `(menu, item)` pair
it is keyed by. The menu is also in the path; both are read from the body so this route and the
`PUT` share one builder.

Flat rather than `#[serde(flatten)]` for the same reason as [`CreateLayoutButtonRequest`].

CreateRecipeRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/inventory/recipes` body: a recipe plus the item it makes.

The item id is in the body here because the collection URI has no room for it, and the `PUT`
keeps taking it from the path. A struct of its own rather than an `Option` on `RecipeRequest`,
so neither route carries a field the other requires — and flat rather than
`#[serde(flatten)]` for the same reason as [`CreateLayoutButtonRequest`].

CreateReleaseRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config-releases` body: the name, the cohort, and the moment. No nodes — those arrive at
schedule time, with the store list, because both are snapshotted then (ADR-0125 §3).

instant_at_ms.description:
A single instant instead, for a release timed in UTC. The escape hatch for a store being set
up: it needs no published `locale` and is always available.

target_group_id.description:
The cohort this release is aimed at, recorded for the report. Optional: a release may name
its stores explicitly at schedule time instead.

wall_clock_date.description:
The operator's local date and time — "Monday 04:00, local". Converted to one instant per
store at schedule time (ADR-0125 §2).

CreateRoleRequest.description: Create a role template — a named subset of the `pos-core` permission catalogue (§9).

discount_ceiling_minor.description:
How much this role may discount before it needs a manager, in the currency's minor unit.
Absent leaves the role with no configured ceiling, which the edge reads as zero — every
discount then needs a manager, exactly as it does today.

permissions.description: What the role grants directly, stored as sent.

permissions_with_approval.description:
What the role grants only with approval (ADR-0158 decision 4), checked by
[`granted_with_approval`]. Absent is none: every permission in `permissions` is granted
directly, as before the list existed.

The catalogue's PIN flag, the default a new role starts from, is the console's to apply: its
role editor starts a newly ticked PIN-flagged permission with approval and always sends both
lists. Applied here, it would give a role created by a script or an old console tab holders
who can no longer approve, since only a direct holder approves, and a `permissions` that
reads back without the ids it was sent.

late_after_seconds.description:
When the station's tickets are late, in seconds; absent or `null` for the default. Read as
any integer so that one out of bounds is refused naming the field, as one too large is.

ticket_language.description:
The language its kitchen tickets print in, as a `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_…` token; absent or `null`
for the store's display language.

CreateStoreGroupRequest.description: A `POST /admin/store-groups` body. The id is server-minted.

language.description:
The language the tenant's starting roles are named in, a language tag such as `vi`. The
console sends the one it is shown in. Absent, or one the console's language packs do not
carry, names them in English. Nothing about the tenant records it.

CreateTerminalRequest.description: An operator names a POS terminal that exists because somebody carried it into the shop.

name.description: What to call it on screen when it is the machine that went quiet.

store_id.description: The store the terminal stands in (a ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant the store belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

CreateTerminalResponse.description: The id a freshly created terminal was given.

id.description: The terminal's device id (a ULID) — what a printer names to make it its agent.

status.description:
`approved`, always: a terminal is created resolved, because the console write *is* the
decision.

CreatedId.description:
What a create answers when its record is not returned: the id it minted.

An entity whose update payload does not carry every field answers its create with this rather
than a representation it would have to invent (`conditional::with_etag` says why); the `ETag`
header carries the version.

id.description: The new record's id, a ULID.

CurrencyCode.description: An ISO 4217 currency code: three upper-case letters

DailyCash.description:
A day's **cash-drawer** summary for one store, folded from the shift and drawer events
([ADR-0081](../../../docs/adr/0081-reports-and-analytics.md), Track O4). Amounts are the store's
single currency's minor units. Part of an X/Z report; T2 (it exposes money).

by_drawer.description:
The same figures for each drawer, keyed by the till's `terminal_device_id`, or by
[`STORE_DRAWER`] for the store's one drawer
([ADR-0167](../../../docs/adr/0167-a-till-has-its-own-cash-drawer.md) decisions 10 and 13).
Each drawer's are the sums of its own events, which are the events the store's figures sum,
so the drawers add up to the store.

`#[serde(default)]`, so a day stored before this field loads with no drawers and gains them
from the rollup's cursor forward. Resetting the rollup (the ADR-0036 reset-cursor-and-replay
lever) folds every cash event on the log into it.

counted.description: Sum of counted amounts across closes (the blind counts).

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 code, or empty until a cash event on the day sets it.

expected.description: Sum of expected drawer amounts across closes.

opening_float.description: Sum of opening floats across shifts opened on the day.

variance.description: Sum of variance (counted − expected) across closes; negative is short.

DailyRevenue.description:
A day's **revenue** for one store, folded from the settlement and line events
([ADR-0081](../../../docs/adr/0081-reports-and-analytics.md), Track O4).

Revenue is recognised from `billing.bill.settled` (the settled totals); the product mix is the
**gross ordered** mix from `sales.order_line.added` — units and value as ordered, **before** voids
and comps are netted (which the line events do not carry back to a menu item), so it reads menu
popularity, not per-item recognised revenue. All amounts are the store's single currency's minor
units (`docs/pos-spec.md` §19). Prices are **T2**: this rollup, and every route that serves it, is
gated behind `console.reports.revenue`. It carries no customer or employee identifier.

by_fee.description:
The fees the day's settled bills charged, keyed by the fee's `code` and ordered by it
([ADR-0159](../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md) decision 4).

Folded from each `billing.bill.settled`'s `fee_lines`, whose amounts sum to that bill's
`service_charge`. So on a day whose every bill recorded its fee lines, these amounts sum to
[`service_charge`](Self::service_charge). A bill settled by an edge from before fee lines
records none, and adds to `service_charge` alone. There is no entry for that difference: a
bucket for it would read as a fee nobody wrote, so the gap is left as the gap between the
two figures.

Bounded by the store's fee rules, not by its trade: one entry per code a rule charged that
day, and the cloud refuses a second active fee under a code a store already runs
(`pos_cloud::fees::shares_code_with`).

`#[serde(default)]`, so a day stored before this field loads with no fees and gains them
from the rollup's cursor forward. Resetting the rollup (the ADR-0036 reset-cursor-and-replay
lever) folds every settled bill on the log into it.

by_item.description: Gross ordered mix, keyed by `menu_item_id`, ordered by key for determinism.

by_tax_component.description:
The tax the day's settled bills recorded by tax component, one entry per component name and
rate, in order of name and then rate
([ADR-0168](../../../docs/adr/0168-a-settled-bill-records-its-tax-components.md) decision 5).

Folded from each `billing.bill.settled`'s tax lines' `components` alone, never from its fee
lines' `tax_components`, because a fee's tax is already inside the tax lines as its share of
its class's tax, and folding both would count it twice.

So on a day whose every bill recorded its components, these sum to [`tax`](Self::tax). A
bill that recorded none adds to `tax` alone: one settled before its edge recorded them, one
taxed at rates with no components, as every Vietnamese and Japanese bill is, and one whose
names are not tokens, which reads as not split. There is no entry for that difference: a
bucket for it would read as a component no bill named, so the gap is left as the gap between
the two figures, as it is for [`by_fee`](Self::by_fee).

Bounded by the tenant's tax table, not by the store's trade: one entry per component name and
rate a row of the table in force named that day.

Left out when empty, so a day with none serialises byte for byte as before this field, and
`#[serde(default)]`, so a day stored before it loads with none and gains them from the
rollup's cursor forward. Resetting the rollup re-folds every settled bill on the log into it.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 code of the store's currency, or empty until the first settled bill sets it.

gross.description: Sum of settled subtotals (before reductions), minor units.

net.description: Sum of `total_due` — what guests owed — minor units. The headline "revenue" figure.

reductions.description: Sum of reductions (discounts + comps), minor units.

service_charge.description: Sum of service charge, minor units.

DailyRollup.description:
A day's activity for one store, derived from the event log.

The cloud's dashboards answer from rollups rather than by scanning the raw log
(`docs/roadmap.md` P7). This first rollup counts events per store trading day and per event
type — enough for an activity dashboard, and it uses only envelope fields (`business_date`,
`event_type`), so it needs no per-event-type decoding. Money- and order-shaped rollups, and the
materialised tables that make the <10 ms dashboard query real, land with the dashboard slice.

by_type.description: Per-event-type counts, ordered by type so the output is deterministic.

total_events.description: Every event recorded on that day.

DeviceId.description: A `DeviceId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DeviceProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal sits in the approval workflow.

DeviceProposalSummary.description: A proposal as listed — the durable facts plus its status.

agent_device_id.description:
The `terminal` device whose transport reaches this printer, if an operator has picked one
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)). `None` — the ordinary case — means the
edge opens the address itself, exactly as it always has.

connection.description:
How the device is attached (`usb`/`network`/`serial`), as approval recorded it — `None` while
pending, because discovery cannot find this out ([ADR-0100](../../../docs/adr/0100-receipt-and-ticket-printing.md)).

cuts_paper.description:
Whether an operator says this printer cuts its paper. `None` until somebody says, which the
edge reads as `true`.

drawer_attached.description:
Whether an operator has marked a cash drawer as wired to this printer
([ADR-0165](../../../docs/adr/0165-cash-paid-in-and-out-is-counted-in-the-drawer-and-a-no-sale-opening-needs-a-manager.md)).
`false` until somebody does, which is what every store assumed before the mark existed.

id.description: The proposal id (a ULID string).

opening_float_minor.description:
On a `terminal`, the float an operator says this till's drawer opens with by default, in the
store currency's minor unit
([ADR-0167](../../../docs/adr/0167-a-till-has-its-own-cash-drawer.md) decision 4). `None`
until somebody says, which is the store's `shift.opening_float_minor`.

paper_width.description:
The paper an operator says this printer takes, as its wire token (`PAPER_WIDTH_…`,
[ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 2). `None` until somebody says, which the edge reads as 80 mm paper: what every
store assumed before the field existed.

receipt_language.description:
On a `terminal`, the language an operator says this till's receipts print in, as its wire
token (`RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_…`). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's.

receipt_printer_id.description:
On a `terminal`, the printer an operator says this till's receipts, receipt copies and
pre-bills go to (a ULID string,
[ADR-0160](../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 4). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's receipt printer.

receipt_second_language.description:
On a `terminal`, the second language an operator says this till's receipts print in, as its
wire token (`RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_…`). `None` until somebody says, which is the store's.

station_id.description:
The kitchen station this device serves, as approval recorded it. `None` for the counter's
receipt printer, which serves the bill rather than a station — and `None` while pending.

store_id.description: The store the device belongs to (a ULID string).

version.description:
The version the row was read at, for a conditional write
([ADR-0094](../../../docs/adr/0094-console-optimistic-concurrency.md)). Opaque: the adapter
mints it from `xmin::text`, and nothing above this seam may assume that.

DeviceRecord.description:
A device — the canonical device identity, grouped under a store. Shares its `device_id` with
`device_proposals` / `device_credentials`.

store_id.description: The owning store.

DevicesPublished.description:
What a devices publish answers: the version it made, how many devices it carries, and how many
approved proposals it left out.

config_version_id.description: The new config version, a ULID.

device_count.description: How many devices the store's node now names.

skipped_count.description: How many it considered and left out.

DisplayCategoryId.description: A `DisplayCategoryId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DisplayName.description:
A human-readable name for a product, category, modifier or campaign.

Tenant content, resolved per language in the configuration tree. Admissible in an
event payload because a line snapshot must capture the name shown to the guest at
the moment the line was added — changing or deleting a menu item afterwards must
not alter an open order or a settled bill.

DisplaySubcategoryId.description: A `DisplaySubcategoryId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

EffectiveFee.description: One fee as one store runs it, and where its rule comes from.

faults.description: Why the store cannot apply it, if it cannot.

published.description: The rule as the store is sent it, its categories compiled into items.

rule.description: The rule as written: the wire rule's fields, and the categories it names.

scope.description: The scope of the rule in force, and what it was written for.

EffectiveFees.description:
What one store's effective fees answer: each fee it runs, and whether all of them can be
published to it.

fees.description: Each fee in force at the store.

publishable.description: Whether no fee has a fault, so a publish would apply them all.

store_id.description: The store, a ULID.

EffectiveSetting.description: One setting as one store runs it, and where its value comes from.

scope.description: The scope that set it, or absent when the store runs the default.

scope_id.description: The tenant, brand, store group or store that set it.

EffectiveSettings.description: What a store's effective settings answer: each setting as the store runs it.

settings.description: One per setting, with the scope its value came from.

Employee.description:
An employee as the console reads them. Note what is **absent**: no PIN and no PIN hash — a read
exposes only `has_pin`, whether a PIN is set, so the directory never becomes a way to exfiltrate
credentials. Serializes for the `/admin` read (a later slice).

code.description: The staff/badge code an operator types — unique within the tenant.

has_pin.description: Whether a sign-in PIN is set. The hash itself is never read out.

EmployeeId.description:
An employee's identifier — a ULID minted at creation. Defined here beside the seam, like
[`BrandId`](crate::registry::BrandId): an employee is a cloud-only concept, so it needs no
`pos-proto` id type.

Enrolment.description:
The TOTP enrolment returned once on a successful first-boot: the `otpauth://` URI an authenticator
app imports (as a QR or by paste) and the raw base32 secret for manual entry.

Both fields carry the shared secret, so [`fmt::Debug`] redacts them — the value reaches the
operator through the HTTP response body, never a log.

secret_base32.description: The base32-encoded shared secret, for an authenticator that takes a typed key.

EntityStatus.description:
Whether an entity is in use or has been retired. Entities are **archived, never hard-deleted**, so
foreign references (a store's config tree, a device's credentials) and history stay valid.

ErrorBody.description: The error body — the schema mirror of [`pos_proto::error::ErrorBody`].

code.description: The HTTP status code, repeated here so a body is self-describing once logged.

details.description: Field-level detail. Absent when the failure is not about a particular field.

message.description: A human-readable explanation. Never contains personal data, because responses are logged.

ErrorDetail.description:
One reason a request failed, tied to the field responsible — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorDetail`].

field.description:
The offending field, in the same `snake_case` name the request used. For a whole-request
fault this can be a header name (`if-match`) rather than a body field.

reason.description:
A stable, machine-readable reason such as `MUST_BE_POSITIVE` or `INVALID_ENUM_VALUE`. Stable
so a client can branch on it; `message` is for people and may be reworded at any time.

ErrorResponse.description:
The envelope every `/admin` failure carries — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorResponse`].

One level of nesting so a response is unambiguous at the top level: a success body is the record,
a failure body is `{"error": …}`.

FeeCode.description:
A short, stable, language-independent handle for a fee, such as `"SERVICE"` or `"PACKAGING"`.

What a report groups fees by and a CSV export prints, so an operator reads a handle they chose
rather than a ULID. Unlike [`crate::reason_codes::ReasonCode`], which no event carries, it is
admissible in an event payload ([`crate::pii`]): ADR-0159 has a bill record the code of every
fee it was charged, in its frozen rules (decision 3) and its settled fee lines (decision 4). It
names a charge, as a [`DisplayName`] names a product, and never a person.

FeeFaultView.description: One rule a store cannot apply, as a refused publish reports it: by id, never by name.

FeeId.description: A `FeeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

FeePublishOutcome.description: How one store's fee publish went, as its token.

FeePublishResult.description: How one store's fee publish went.

faults.description: For a refused store: each rule it cannot apply, and why.

FeeRuleBody.description:
A rule as the console sends it: the wire rule's own fields, with each id as text so a malformed
one is refused by name, and the item categories an include or exclude list names besides its
items. A field left out takes the default the owner confirmed: after discounts, net of tax,
taxed the way its lines are, not waivable, on every channel and every item, and active.

fee_id.description: The fee: absent on a `POST`, which mints its id, and the fee written on a `PUT`.

FeeRuleRequest.description: A `POST` or `PUT /admin/fees` body: one rule, at one scope.

scope_id.description: The tenant, brand or store the rule is for.

FeeRuleView.description: One rule as the console lists it.

rule.description: The rule as written: the wire rule's fields, and the categories it names.

scope_id.description: The tenant, brand or store it was written for.

updated_by.description: The console admin who last wrote it, by id.

FeeRules.description: What the fee list answers: every rule the tenant wrote.

rules.description: The rules, each with its scope and who last wrote it.

FeeTotal.description: One fee's total on a trading day, under its code (part of [`DailyRevenue`]).

amount.description: Sum of what the fee charged, minor units.

bills.description: Settled bills that charged the fee.

name.description: The most recent name a settled bill recorded for the fee, for a human-readable report.

tax.description: Sum of the tax on it, minor units.

FeeWritten.description: What a fee write answers: the fee it wrote, and how publishing to each store it reached went.

fee_id.description: The fee's id, a ULID: the one sent, or the one minted for a new fee.

stores.description: One result per store the write reached.

FetchReleaseRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/ota/releases/fetch` body: which version to go and get.

`release` is spelled the way the registry keys it and a rollout's `target_version` names it —
bare, without a leading `v` ([ADR-0088](../../../docs/adr/0088-ota-artifact-hosting.md)
Amendment 2). Which tag that is on the forge is the source's business, and it tries both.

FetchedArtifactResponse.description: One artifact the fetch put in the cloud.

asset.description: The asset the bytes came from, so the console can say what it took.

outcome.description: Whether the cloud stored it now or already held these exact bytes.

FieldView.description: One field of a provider's settings schema.

FleetPrintAgent.description:
One bound print agent as the fleet console sees it
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)).

Two opaque identifiers and a duration, carried verbatim from what the store reported. No document,
no line, no name: nothing a ticket *says* helps diagnose a stalled agent, so nothing a ticket says
crosses this wire either.

agent_device_id.description: The terminal a console admin created and a manager bound at the till.

oldest_unacknowledged_secs.description:
How long the oldest still-unacknowledged job has waited, or `null` when nothing is waiting.
`null` is the healthy answer and is deliberately not zero.

paired_device_id.description: The paired device answering for it — the box an operator has to walk to.

FleetStoreView.description:
One store as the fleet console sees it: the seam's raw facts plus the two verdicts derived at read
time — `online` (from `last_seen_at` against [`FLEET_ONLINE_THRESHOLD_MS`]) and `config_current`
