(the held version equals the published one). Timestamps are Unix milliseconds, the shape the
dashboard reads; the store id is a string so the console shows a name and hides the ULID.

edge_placement.description:
Where the machine holding the authoritative generation runs — the `EDGE_PLACEMENT_*` token,
or `null` ([ADR-0110](../../../docs/adr/0110-edge-placement-is-a-deployment-axis.md)).

`null` covers two different things on purpose, and the console must not read it as a mode:
the cloud has never bumped this store, or the stored token is one this build cannot decode.
Neither is `EDGE_PLACEMENT_UNSPECIFIED` — on the wire that token means *this message did not
say*, and a server that emitted it would be saying something. A field that is simply absent
is the honest shape for both.

What the two absences mean for *urgency* is deliberately not on this view, because the
console does not decide it: the alert engine reads the same `FleetRow` and scores an
undecodable token with the hosted case rather than the in-store one.

handover.description:
Which state this store's handover is in — `taking-over`, `settled`, `retired` — or `null`
when it has never had one
([ADR-0110](../../../docs/adr/0110-edge-placement-is-a-deployment-axis.md)).

Derived here, not stored, exactly as `online` and `config_current` are, and by
[`handover_state`] so the console never re-implements the rule — in particular the same-beat
guard, which is the half that is easy to get wrong and expensive to get wrong.

`null` is a real answer and the commonest one: a store on generation `0` has never been
replaced, and a store with no lease row has never been issued one. Neither is a handover in
any state, so the console renders no badge rather than a reassuring one.

installed_version.description:
The binary version the store last reported running (ADR-0078), or `null` if it has never
reported.

lease_generation_authoritative.description: The store's authoritative lease generation, or `null` if the cloud has never issued it one.

lease_generation_held.description:
The lease generation the box last reported holding
([ADR-0108](../../../docs/adr/0108-the-lease-generation-is-authority.md)), or `null` if it
has never said.

lease_reported_at_ms.description: Unix ms of the heartbeat that reported it, or `null`.

lease_superseded.description:
Whether this box has been **superseded**: it holds a generation the store has moved past, so
it refuses over-the-air updates and is no longer the machine the store runs on.

Derived here rather than stored, exactly as `online` and `config_current` are: it is a
comparison of two numbers the row already carries, and deriving it in one place keeps the
console from re-implementing `lease_standing` in TypeScript. `false` when either number is
absent — a store with no lease in force, or a box that has not reported one, is not
*superseded*; it is simply not under the lease yet, and saying otherwise would put a red
badge on every store the day this shipped.

lease_superseded_generation.description:
The generation the last bump displaced and nothing has yet proved drained, or `null`
([ADR-0110](../../../docs/adr/0110-edge-placement-is-a-deployment-axis.md)).

Shown beside [`handover`](Self::handover) rather than in place of it: the state says *what*
is happening and this says *which machine* it is about, which is the number an operator needs
to type into a settle.

outbox_depth.description:
How many events the store had committed and not yet published as of its last heartbeat, or
`null` if it has never reported one. The mirror of `relay_backlog`: that counts orders held
*for* the store, this counts sales held *at* it. `null` is not zero — a store that never said
is not a store that is caught up — so the console renders the two differently.

outbox_reported_at_ms.description: Unix ms of the heartbeat that reported `outbox_depth`, or `null`.

print_agents.description:
The print agents the store last reported, or `null` if it never has
([ADR-0112](../../../docs/adr/0112-print-agents.md)).

`null` and `[]` are different answers and the console renders them differently: `null` is a
store that has said nothing about agents — every store whose edge runs in the shop, and every
edge on a binary older than this field — while `[]` is a store that looked and has none.

print_agents_reported_at_ms.description:
Unix ms of the heartbeat that reported them, or `null`. A standing is only as current as the
beat that carried it, so the instant travels with the list.

profile_country.description:
The country this store publishes in its `locale` node
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

**Present only on the single-store read**, which is the one route that loads a store's
configuration; the listing omits the key entirely rather than sending `null`, so a console
can tell "not compared here" from "compared, and there is no country". Absence must never
render as agreement.

region_acknowledgement.description:
The answer somebody recorded for **this** difference, or absent
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

Present only when a stored acknowledgement names the same two country codes the store has
right now. An answer written about a difference the store no longer has is not returned —
see [`standing_acknowledgement`] — so a console that renders "acknowledged" whenever this key
is present is correct without knowing the rule.

Omitted on the listing with the two fields above it, for the same reason.

region_agreement.description:
Whether the region agrees with that country — `agrees`, `differs`, `country-not-recorded` —
or absent when there is nothing to compare
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

Derived by [`region_agreement`] rather than in the console, for the reason `handover` beside
it is: the third case is the one that is easy to get wrong, and getting it wrong means a
store with no recorded country renders as agreeing.

Omitted on the listing, exactly as [`profile_country`](Self::profile_country) is — a
comparison there would be one config-tree load per row.

region_country.description:
Where in the world that machine is — its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country — or `null`
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

`null` for a store nobody has bumped, for one whose edge placement is in-store (the machine
is in the shop and has no region), and for a row written before migration `0058`. All three
mean the same thing to a reader — there is nothing to show — which is why this is a plain
`Option` and the placement beside it is not.

region_label.description:
The place a person recognises — `ap-southeast-1`, `Ho Chi Minh City`, `the rack in Sakai` —
or `null`. Present exactly when [`region_country`](Self::region_country) is.

Free text an admin typed, carried verbatim and never parsed. It is on this read because the
question it answers ("where has this store been running?") is asked while somebody has the
fleet page open, not afterwards.

reported_at_ms.description: Unix ms of the store's most recent OTA report, or `null`.

retired_at_ms.description: When a person decided this handover's outgoing machine is no longer needed, or `null`.

retired_by.description:
The deciding admin's id, or `null`.

An id, and the console resolves it to a name through the admin roster if it wants one. The
email lives in the audit trail, which is read under a permission this view is not behind.

self_test_ok.description: Whether the store's last post-install self-test passed, or `null`.

FloorRoutingRule.description:
An item→station routing rule as the console reads it. Matches a specific item or any line on a
course (the route layer enforces exactly one); `sort` orders rules within their tier.

oneOf.description: The course this rule matches, if any.
The item this rule matches, if any.

sort.description: The author-controlled order within its tier.

station_id.description: The station a matching line routes to.

store_id.description: The store this rule belongs to.

FreeFormJson.description: Free-form JSON. The route's description names what it is and where its shape is defined

GenerateVouchersRequest.description: A `POST /admin/campaigns/{id}/vouchers` body: the tenant and how many codes to mint.

GridPosition.description: Where a button sits on a POS terminal's fixed grid: zero-based `column` and `row`.

HaltRolloutRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/ota/halt` body: the `(tenant, store)` whose rollout to halt (`true`) or
resume (`false`) — the kill switch, without re-typing the whole rollout.

HostedArtifactResponse.description: One hosted artifact, as the console reads it.

ImportReport.description: The dry-run (and post-apply) report: every row's fate plus the totals the UI headlines.

create_count.description: How many rows would be created.

rows.description: One entry per data row, in file order.

update_count.description: How many rows would overwrite an existing key.

allOf.description: The classification.

key.description: The content key the row is for (may be empty for a rejected blank-key row).

ImportRow.description: One row's key and what would happen to it.

IngredientId.description: A `IngredientId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

IngredientRequest.description:
A create/update body for an ingredient. The id is **server-owned** — minted on create, the path id
on update — so a client never supplies or forges it. `name` and `unit` are the wire ingredient's own
fields, reused rather than re-declared.

IntegrationsPublished.description: What an integrations publish answers: the version it made, and how many connections it carries.

config_version_id.description: The new config version, a ULID.

integrations.description: How many connections the store's node now names.

InviteAdminRequest.description: A request to invite a new console admin.

email.description: The invitee's email — the address they will sign in with (normalised server-side).

role.description: The role to grant on acceptance: `owner`/`admin`/`ops`/`viewer`.

InviteAdminResponse.description:
The one-time response to an invitation: the id, the single-use token (shown once) the inviter
copies into the invite link, and the expiry. Only the token's hash is stored.

expires_at_ms.description: When the invite stops being acceptable (Unix milliseconds).

token.description:
The single-use invite token. **Shown once** — only its hash is stored, so it cannot be
recovered later; the inviter hands the link carrying it to the invitee out-of-band.

IssueActivationRequest.description: A super-admin issues an activation code for a device slot.

device_id.description: The device slot to activate (a ULID).

store_id.description: The store the device belongs to (a ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant the device belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

IssueActivationResponse.description: The freshly-issued code, shown once for the operator to put on the setup sheet.

activation_code.description: The `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` code — the only time it is visible; only its hash is stored.

ItemCategory.description:
An item category — the operational taxonomy for reporting, tax defaults and kitchen grouping
(ADR-0066 entity 2). This is **not** the presentation taxonomy a screen groups by (that is a
[display category](DisplayCategory-like) delivered in the layout, entity 11); a product-mix report
groups by *this*.

ItemCategoryId.description:
An item category's identifier — a ULID minted at creation. The operational taxonomy is a
cloud-authoring concept (reporting/tax-default/kitchen grouping); like [`MenuId`], its id is
defined beside the seam rather than in [`pos_proto::ids`].

ItemMix.description: One menu item's gross ordered contribution on a trading day (part of [`DailyRevenue`]).

name.description: The most recent display name seen for the item, for a human-readable report.

ordered_qty_milli.description: Sum of ordered quantity, in thousandths of a unit (`Quantity::milli`).

ordered_value.description: Sum of ordered line totals, minor units — gross, before voids/comps.

ItemSubcategory.description: An item sub-category — a refinement of an [`ItemCategory`] (ADR-0066 entity 3).

ItemSubcategoryId.description: An item sub-category's identifier — a ULID minted at creation, nested under an [`ItemCategoryId`].

LayoutButton.description:
One item's button in a per-channel layout — the authoring row a compiled [`pos_proto::DisplayButton`]
is made from (ADR-0066 entity 12).

A "layout" is the set of these rows for a channel: the compiler groups them by
`(sales_channel → display category → sub-category)`, orders each group by `sort`, and emits a
[`pos_proto::DisplayPlan`] per channel into a [`pos_proto::LayoutBook`]. Its identity is
`(tenant, sales_channel, menu_item_id)` — an item has at most one button per channel. Presentation
only: it names an item's `menu_item_id` and where its button sits, never a price.

display_category_id.description: The display category the button sits under.

oneOf.description: The sub-category within that category, or `None` for a button directly under the category.

label.description: The caption to show (may be shorter than the item's catalog name on a crowded grid).

menu_item_id.description: The item this button orders — a `menu_item_id` the compiled `MenuBook` prices.

oneOf.description: The button's grid slot on a POS terminal, or `None` for a flowing layout (tablet, QR).

sales_channel.description: The channel this button lays out. `Open`, like [`ChannelPrice::sales_channel`].

sort.description: The display order within its group; lower comes first.

LeaseRead.description: What the lease read answers: the store's authoritative generation.

generation.description: The generation, or `null` when the store was never issued one.

items.description:
One audit entry as the console reads it: ids as strings (the screen shows names/labels, not raw
ULIDs front-and-centre), the actor snapshot flattened, and the instant as Unix ms.

oneOf.description: The whole set, when the caller named no `limit`.
One page, when it did.

ListOrPage_AuditEntryView.description:
What a list route that pages answers, as its OpenAPI schema names it: the whole set as an array
without `limit`, or a [`PagedBody`] with one (ADR-0098).

The handler answers with one or the other through [`paged_ok`] or a plain `Json`; this type
only describes the two shapes as one `oneOf`. [`list_or_page_tests`] holds each variant to the
bytes the handler's own answer serialises to.

items.description: One media asset as listed — id, content type, the detail rendition's size, and when it was stored.

oneOf.description: The whole set, when the caller named no `limit`.
One page, when it did.

ListOrPage_MediaSummaryView.description:
What a list route that pages answers, as its OpenAPI schema names it: the whole set as an array
without `limit`, or a [`PagedBody`] with one (ADR-0098).

The handler answers with one or the other through [`paged_ok`] or a plain `Json`; this type
only describes the two shapes as one `oneOf`. [`list_or_page_tests`] holds each variant to the
bytes the handler's own answer serialises to.

allOf.description:
An item in the catalog — the product master.

Its id is a [`MenuItemId`], the same identifier the compiled [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`] names and an
inbound order references: the item authored here is the item priced downstream. This slice carries
the fields a `MenuEntry` needs (name, tax class); its operational category, recipe/BOM link and
the rest arrive with later slices.

oneOf.description:
The course this item goes out on, or `None` for an item on no course
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md) decision 3).

Carried on the item exactly as [`tax_class_id`](Self::tax_class_id) is, and for the same
reason: a pizza is a main, and making a server say so on every tap would be a tap per dish
for a fact the catalog already knows. `None` is every item in every store today and stays
correct.

A **per-line override** is deliberately not modelled. The request it would serve — *"bring my
main with the starters"* — is about when the food goes, and firing already answers that;
relabelling a line's course to mean "sooner" would put a timing decision inside a taxonomy.

The item's photo — a [`MediaId`] into the media library (ADR-0075), or `None`. Authoring/display
only; it does not cross to the edge. A dangling ref (the asset was deleted) shows a placeholder.
The operational category this item reports under, or `None` if unclassified (entity 2).
The operational sub-category, refining the category, or `None` (entity 3).

menu_item_id.description: The item's id — shared with the compiled menu entry and any inbound order that names it.

name.description:
The human name (the default caption, before a layout overrides it per channel). Always
present, and the fallback for a locale [`name_translations`](Self::name_translations) omits.

name_translations.description:
The item's name in each locale it is translated into, keyed by locale code (`"vi"`, `"en"`, …)
([ADR-0074](../../../docs/adr/0074-localization-and-tax.md), Track M4). The compiler carries
these onto the [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`]; the store's display language selects one at the edge,
falling back to [`name`](Self::name). Additive — an item with none behaves as before.

tax_class_id.description: The tax class, which the store's channel-keyed rate table turns into a rate at reprice time.

etag.description:
The version [`record`](Self::record) was read at. Byte-identical to the `ETag` header
a single-resource read would carry, so a client never reformats it.

updated_at_ms.description:
When the row was last written, in Unix milliseconds — `None` where the adapter does not
project it.

Every one of these tables has carried an `updated_at` since it was created; not one read
ever returned it, so the console had no way to tell an operator whether what is on their
screen is newer than what the shop is running. The publish bar asked that question and had
to answer it from a within-session signal, which forgets on reload (Wave 4 · PR-5b, F13).

`Option` and skipped when absent, so this is additive twice over: the 80-odd existing
[`new`](Self::new) call sites compile untouched, and a read that does not project the
column serialises exactly the bytes it did before.

items.description:
A record together with the version it was read at.

Serialises as the record's own fields plus an `etag` — additive, so no existing field
moves or is renamed, and a list can carry a version per row where a header cannot.

Serialize only. This shape is something the cloud *writes*; the console reads it in TypeScript,
and no Rust caller parses one. Deriving `Deserialize` as well would pull in serde's flatten
buffer, whose `Content` enum carries `f32`/`f64` variants that `clippy.toml` bans outright —
a real cost (`docs/adr/0013`: money is never a float) for a capability nothing uses.

oneOf.description: The whole set, when the caller named no `limit`.
One page, when it did.

code.description: The staff/badge code an operator types — unique within the tenant.

has_pin.description: Whether a sign-in PIN is set. The hash itself is never read out.

a single-resource read would carry, so a client never reformats it.
