ListOrPage_Versioned_Employee.description:
What a list route that pages answers, as its OpenAPI schema names it: the whole set as an array
without `limit`, or a [`PagedBody`] with one (ADR-0098).

The handler answers with one or the other through [`paged_ok`] or a plain `Json`; this type
only describes the two shapes as one `oneOf`. [`list_or_page_tests`] holds each variant to the
bytes the handler's own answer serialises to.

LoginRequest.description:
An admin sign-in request: who is signing in, their password, and the current TOTP code.

`email` is **optional**, and that is the one load-bearing choice in
[ADR-0119](../../../../docs/adr/0119-each-admin-signs-in-as-themselves.md). Migration 0018 gave the
only admin every existing installation has a synthetic, non-routable address
([`IMPLICIT_OWNER_EMAIL`]) that nobody has seen and no route can change, so requiring the field
would lock out every installation on the day this deployed. Absent, it resolves to the single
admin when there is exactly one — which is every installation today — and is refused once there
are two, which is exactly when guessing would start being wrong.

[`fmt::Debug`] redacts the password and any recovery code, so a logged request cannot leak either.
The email is not redacted: it is the identity, and it is what the log needs to attribute a failed
attempt.

email.description: Who is signing in. Absent resolves to the single admin; see the type's own note.

recovery_code.description:
A one-time recovery code, used in place of the TOTP second factor when the authenticator is
lost ([ADR-0067](../../../../docs/adr/0067-multi-admin-console-rbac.md) slice 6). Absent for an
ordinary password + TOTP sign-in.

totp_code.description: The current 6-digit TOTP code. Ignored when a `recovery_code` is present.

MediaId.description:
A media asset's identifier — a ULID minted at upload. Cloud-only: an item or brand references it
(`image_ref`), but it never crosses the edge wire, so it lives beside the seam like
[`MenuId`](crate::catalog::Menu) rather than in `pos-proto`. Serializes as its bare ULID string, so
an item's/brand's `image_ref` is a plain id (or `null`) on the admin API.

MediaSummaryView.description: One media asset as listed — id, content type, the detail rendition's size, and when it was stored.

Menu.description:
A menu — a named set of placements that may **inherit** from a parent menu.

Inheritance is how a brand menu overrides a tenant standard and a store special overrides the
brand: the compiler folds a parent's placements under a child's, most-specific-wins. A cycle in
`parent_menu_id` is a configuration error the compiler rejects; the seam only stores the edge.

oneOf.description: The menu this one inherits from, or `None` for a root menu.

MenuId.description:
A menu's identifier — a ULID minted at creation. A menu is an authoring concept that never
crosses the wire (the compiled [`pos_proto::MenuBook`] has no menu id), so its id is defined here
beside the seam rather than in [`pos_proto::ids`], the same way a `BrandId` is.

MenuItemId.description: A `MenuItemId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

MenuPlacement.description:
An item placed in a menu, with its per-channel prices — the row a compiled `MenuEntry` is made
from. Its identity is the pair `(menu_id, menu_item_id)`: an item appears in a menu at most once.

available.description:
Whether the item is for sale in this menu right now — the operator's *published* floor, which
the edge's live-stock auto-86 (`pos-core` §8) can only push further down, never re-raise.

menu_id.description: The menu this placement belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The section this placement sits under, or `None` for an unsectioned placement. Authoring-only
(ADR-0066 entity 7): it groups the row for the operator, and does not reach the compiled book.

prices.description:
The item's price per channel in this menu. A channel with no row here falls to the menu's
parent (inheritance) or, failing that, is not sold on that channel.

MenuSection.description:
A menu section — an authoring grouping within a menu (ADR-0066 entity 7), e.g. `Starters`, `Mains`,
`Desserts` on a single menu.

A section is where the operator organises a menu's placements for authoring and printing; a
[`MenuPlacement`] carries an optional `menu_section_id` naming the section it sits under. Sections
are **authoring-only**: the compiled `MenuBook` is a flat set of entries, so a section changes what
the operator sees while authoring, never what the edge is served. A [`ModifierGroup`] held the
same posture until [ADR-0127](../../../docs/adr/0127-modifier-groups-reach-the-edge.md) carried it
down; a section has not moved, because nothing at the till asks which section an item was under.

menu_id.description: The menu this section belongs to.

sort.description: Where the section sorts within its menu, ascending. Ties break by id.

MenuSectionId.description:
A menu section's identifier — a ULID minted at creation. A section is an authoring grouping within
a menu (ADR-0066 entity 7); like [`MenuId`] it never crosses the wire (the compiled `MenuBook` is a
flat list of entries with no sections), so its id lives beside the seam.

MissingPermission.description: One catalogue permission a role grants neither directly nor with approval.

id.description: The permission's `domain.resource.action` id.

ModifierGroup.description:
A modifier group — a set of modifier choices with a min/max selection rule, attached to items
(ADR-0066 entities 4 and 5).

A **modifier is itself an item** (a [`MenuItemId`] priced in the same money, ADR-0063), so this
entity needs no separate modifier type: `member_item_ids` are the items offered as choices, and
`attached_item_ids` are the items this group modifies (a pizza's "Size", "Extra toppings"). The
selection rule is `min_select..=max_select`.

This is the **authoring** shape, and it reaches a store compiled
([ADR-0127](../../../docs/adr/0127-modifier-groups-reach-the-edge.md)):
[`crate::catalog_compiler::compile_menu`] inverts the attachment — the operator pins one group to
forty pizzas, the till asks the opposite question once per tap — and emits a
[`pos_proto::MenuModifierGroup`] carrying the rule, the name and the members, with no `tenant_id`,
`etag` or `status`. An archived group is simply not published.

attached_item_ids.description: The items this group is attached to (the products that show this modifier set).

max_select.description: The maximum number of choices a guest may select.

member_item_ids.description: The items offered as choices in this group — each a modifier, i.e. an item.

min_select.description: The minimum number of choices a guest must select (0 for optional).

ModifierGroupId.description: A `ModifierGroupId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

Money.description:
An amount of money: an integer count of the currency's minor unit.

The wire form is `{"currency_code": "VND", "amount_minor": 150000}`, and the
database form is `char(3)` plus `bigint`. Both halves travel together always —
an amount without its currency is not money, it is a number.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units: đồng for VND, yen for JPY, cents for USD.

NodePreview.description: What a preview answers with: the node it compiled, and the diff a publish of it would apply.

diff.description:
The RFC 7386 merge patch the publish would apply to the store's effective document, with its
staff and prices redacted for the caller's role ([`admin_preview_config_node`]).

from_version_id.description: The version the diff is computed against, or `null` when the store has no tree yet.

node.description: Echoed back so a console that fired several previews can tell the answers apart.

unchanged.description: True when nothing would change — there is nothing to publish.

OpenFeeItems_FeeItems.description: A `FeeItems` token: FEE_ITEMS_UNSPECIFIED, FEE_ITEMS_ALL, FEE_ITEMS_INCLUDE, FEE_ITEMS_EXCLUDE, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenFeeKind_FeeKind.description: A `FeeKind` token: FEE_KIND_UNSPECIFIED, FEE_KIND_PERCENT, FEE_KIND_AMOUNT_PER_BILL, FEE_KIND_AMOUNT_PER_UNIT, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenFeeTax_FeeTax.description: A `FeeTax` token: FEE_TAX_UNSPECIFIED, FEE_TAX_NOT_TAXABLE, FEE_TAX_FOLLOW_LINES, FEE_TAX_TAX_CLASS, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenPaymentMethod_PaymentMethod.description: A `PaymentMethod` token: PAYMENT_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED, PAYMENT_METHOD_CASH, PAYMENT_METHOD_CARD, PAYMENT_METHOD_QR, PAYMENT_METHOD_VOUCHER, PAYMENT_METHOD_GIFT_CARD, PAYMENT_METHOD_OTHER, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenReasonAction_ReasonAction.description: A `ReasonAction` token: REASON_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED, REASON_ACTION_VOID_LINE, REASON_ACTION_VOID_BILL, REASON_ACTION_DISCOUNT, REASON_ACTION_COMP, REASON_ACTION_REFUND, REASON_ACTION_DRAWER_OPEN, REASON_ACTION_REJECT_ORDER, REASON_ACTION_CASH_PAID_IN, REASON_ACTION_CASH_PAID_OUT, REASON_ACTION_STOCK_ADJUSTMENT, REASON_ACTION_STOCK_WASTE, REASON_ACTION_WAIVE_FEE, REASON_ACTION_CASH_VARIANCE, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenSalesChannel_SalesChannel.description: A `SalesChannel` token: SALES_CHANNEL_UNSPECIFIED, SALES_CHANNEL_DINE_IN, SALES_CHANNEL_TAKEAWAY, SALES_CHANNEL_DELIVERY, SALES_CHANNEL_QR, SALES_CHANNEL_API, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenSettingScope_SettingScope.description: A `SettingScope` token: SETTING_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED, SETTING_SCOPE_TENANT, SETTING_SCOPE_BRAND, SETTING_SCOPE_STORE_GROUP, SETTING_SCOPE_STORE, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenTableOrder_TableOrder.description: A `TableOrder` token: TABLE_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED, TABLE_ORDER_SEPARATE, TABLE_ORDER_JOIN, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenUnitOfMeasure_UnitOfMeasure.description: A `UnitOfMeasure` token: UNIT_OF_MEASURE_UNSPECIFIED, UNIT_OF_MEASURE_GRAM, UNIT_OF_MEASURE_KILOGRAM, UNIT_OF_MEASURE_MILLILITER, UNIT_OF_MEASURE_LITER, UNIT_OF_MEASURE_PIECE, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenVendorAvailability_VendorAvailabilit.description: A `VendorAvailability` token: VENDOR_AVAILABILITY_UNSPECIFIED, VENDOR_AVAILABILITY_OPEN, VENDOR_AVAILABILITY_BUSY, VENDOR_AVAILABILITY_CLOSED, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

PagedBody_AuditEntryView.description:
A page on the wire: the rows, the size of the whole set, and the bounds that produced them.

The bounds are echoed because a pager needs them to render "1–25 of 812" and to build the next
request, and because the alternative — the client tracking what it sent — breaks the moment a
link is shared or a page is reloaded.

items.description:
One audit entry as the console reads it: ids as strings (the screen shows names/labels, not raw
ULIDs front-and-centre), the actor snapshot flattened, and the instant as Unix ms.

PagedBody_MediaSummaryView.description:
A page on the wire: the rows, the size of the whole set, and the bounds that produced them.

The bounds are echoed because a pager needs them to render "1–25 of 812" and to build the next
request, and because the alternative — the client tracking what it sent — breaks the moment a
link is shared or a page is reloaded.

items.description: One media asset as listed — id, content type, the detail rendition's size, and when it was stored.

PagedBody_Versioned.description:
A page on the wire: the rows, the size of the whole set, and the bounds that produced them.

The bounds are echoed because a pager needs them to render "1–25 of 812" and to build the next
request, and because the alternative — the client tracking what it sent — breaks the moment a
link is shared or a page is reloaded.

allOf.description: The record itself, flattened so the wire shape is unchanged but for `etag`.

etag.description:
The version [`record`](Self::record) was read at. Byte-identical to the `ETag` header
a single-resource read would carry, so a client never reformats it.

updated_at_ms.description:
When the row was last written, in Unix milliseconds — `None` where the adapter does not
project it.

Every one of these tables has carried an `updated_at` since it was created; not one read
ever returned it, so the console had no way to tell an operator whether what is on their
screen is newer than what the shop is running. The publish bar asked that question and had
to answer it from a within-session signal, which forgets on reload (Wave 4 · PR-5b, F13).

`Option` and skipped when absent, so this is additive twice over: the 80-odd existing
[`new`](Self::new) call sites compile untouched, and a read that does not project the
column serialises exactly the bytes it did before.

items.description:
A record together with the version it was read at.

Serialises as the record's own fields plus an `etag` — additive, so no existing field
moves or is renamed, and a list can carry a version per row where a header cannot.

Serialize only. This shape is something the cloud *writes*; the console reads it in TypeScript,
and no Rust caller parses one. Deriving `Deserialize` as well would pull in serde's flatten
buffer, whose `Content` enum carries `f32`/`f64` variants that `clippy.toml` bans outright —
a real cost (`docs/adr/0013`: money is never a float) for a capability nothing uses.

PermissionInfo.description:
One entry of the permission catalogue the console offers when authoring a role. Mirrors the
`pos-core` [`Permission`] metadata (§9) so the console renders permissions grouped, with their
risk and PIN policy, from the framework's own source of truth rather than a hand-kept UI list.

description.description: A one-line description for the dashboard.

group.description: The group token the dashboard groups by (e.g. `BILLING`).

id.description: The stable `domain.resource.action` id a role template stores.

pin_required.description: Whether the permission always demands a PIN at the point of use, whatever the role.

PermissionsPublishOutcome.description: How one store's `permissions` publish went, as its token.

PermissionsPublishResult.description: How one store's `permissions` publish went, as a write that publishes at once reports it.

enforced_scope.description:
The scope of the value the store runs, a `SETTING_SCOPE_*` token, absent when it runs the
default.

enforced_scope_id.description: The tenant, brand, store group or store that value was written for, beside `enforced_scope`.

PresetsApplied.description: What applying a preset answers: the settings it wrote, and how publishing to the store went.

applied.description: The setting keys the preset wrote.

stores.description: One result per store the write reached.

PreviewFeeRule.description: One rule a preview writes in place, as a `PUT` body carries it.

PreviewFeesRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/fees/preview` body: a store, the rules as they would be written, and the lines of
a sample bill.

rules.description:
Rules as a `PUT` would send them, each at its scope, in place of what is written there. A rule
with no `fee_id` is a fee not created yet.

oneOf.description:
The channel the sample bill's order comes in on, which picks the menu's prices, the tax
rate and the fees that apply. Dine-in when absent.

PreviewNodeRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/preview` body — the same `(node, arguments)` pair a batch publish takes,
aimed at one store instead of a cohort.

arguments.description:
That node's own arguments: the single-store publish body minus the `(tenant, store)`.
Nodes compiled from tenant-wide authoring take none, and an object is accepted and ignored.

node.description: Which node to compile — one of the thirteen the registry knows.

ProviderView.description: One provider, with the schema the console draws its form from.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Empty means every country.

PublishCampaignsRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/campaigns` body: the `(tenant, store)` to push the tenant's authored campaigns
to. Like every other node publish, the campaigns come from what is authored, not the body.

PublishCapabilitiesRequest.description:
A super-admin sets a store's capability flags from the form editor: the (tenant, store) and the flag
values to write. Only the flags named are changed; the rest of the store's config is untouched.

flags.description: The capability flag values to set, keyed by each capability's config key (`tables_enabled`, …).

PublishChannelsRequest.description: A `PUT /admin/config/channels` body: the `(tenant, store)` and the enabled sales-channel tokens.

PublishDevicesRequest.description: A super-admin selects the (tenant, store) whose `devices` node to compile and publish.

store_id.description: The store whose approved devices to publish (a 26-character ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant that owns the store (a 26-character ULID).

PublishFeesRequest.description: A `POST /admin/fees/publish` body: the tenant, and one store or, without one, every store.

PublishFloorRequest.description: A super-admin selects the (tenant, store) whose `floor`/`stations` nodes to compile and publish.

PublishIntegrationsRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/integrations` body: the store to publish to. What goes on it is resolved
from the tenant's connections, never sent.

PublishInventoryRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/inventory` body: the `(tenant, store)` to push the tenant's authored inventory
to. Like every other node publish, the ingredients/recipes/suppliers come from what is authored, not
the body.

PublishLocaleRequest.description:
A super-admin sets a store's locale settings: the `(tenant, store)` and the currency, IANA
timezone, and business-date cutoff hour. These drive money display and business-date derivation on
the edge (ADR-0014); until M4 they were hardcoded to VND/UTC/04:00 in the edge bootstrap.

cash_denominations.description:
The notes the till offers as quick-cash keys, in minor units. Absent or empty means the exact
amount only, which is the honest answer rather than a guess.

cash_rounding_increment.description:
What the grand total is rounded to in cash, in minor units — `1000` for Vietnam's thousand
đồng, `100` for India's rupee, absent for Japan
([ADR-0105](../../../docs/adr/0105-a-country-pack-is-values.md)).

country_code.description:
Which country this store is in, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

**Required, and that is a deliberate break** from the shape this route had before. It sits
beside `currency_code` and `timezone` because [D21](../../../docs/roadmap-v3.md) puts all
three in the same place — attributes of a *store* — and this node already carried the other
two. It was simply missing.

Required rather than optional because a publish rebuilds this node wholesale, so an optional
field has only two possible meanings and both are wrong. "Absent clears it" makes an edit to
the cutoff hour erase where a store's data rests, silently. "Absent keeps it" makes this
field behave unlike `display_language` one line down, which *does* clear when omitted — a
trap for the next reader of this struct. Required leaves no absent case at all: a caller
that does not send one is refused by name, loudly, and fixes one line.

`#[serde(default)]` and *not* a bare required field, deliberately. A missing field makes
axum's `Json` extractor answer `422` with its own plain body, which is off the
[AIP-193](../../../docs/naming-and-api.md) envelope the whole `/admin` surface was moved
onto. Defaulting to the empty string routes "absent" through the same check as "malformed",
so both answer one `400` naming `country_code` and saying what it accepts.

display_language.description:
The store's display language (a locale code, e.g. `"vi"`), which selects a compiled item's
per-locale name at the edge (ADR-0074). Optional; when absent or blank the store shows each
item's default name, exactly as before.

prices_include_tax.description:
Whether this store's menu prices already contain their tax
([ADR-0104](../../../docs/adr/0104-multi-component-and-inclusive-tax.md)): Japan's 税込 and
India's MRP are `true`, Vietnam's `++` is `false`. Defaults to `false`, which is what every
store did before the field existed.

PublishMenuRequest.description: A super-admin selects the (tenant, store, menu) to compile and publish.

menu_id.description: The menu to compile — its inheritance chain and placements (a ULID).

store_id.description: The store whose `menu` config node receives the compiled book (a ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant that owns the catalog and the store (a 26-character ULID).

PublishOriginsRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/origins` body: the `(tenant, store)` and the origins that store's edge
answers beside the one that served the request
([ADR-0111](../../../docs/adr/0111-a-second-origin-may-address-the-edge.md)).

The serving origin is never listed here and never needs to be: the edge compares it against the
request's own `Host`, so a store that publishes nothing keeps serving its own UI.

PublishPermissionsRequest.description: A super-admin selects the (tenant, store) whose `permissions` node to compile and publish.

PublishPlacementRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/ota/placement` body: the `(tenant, store)` and where in the rollout it sits —
its ring, and the stable canary bucket that fixes its place in the fleet ramp.

PublishQrRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/qr` body: the store and the QR guardrail settings (P11b/ADR-0057). Composed
into the `qr` node the cloud's QR intake reads (`qr_http::qr_config_for`) and the edge reads for its
staff-confirmation decision.

enabled.description:
QR ordering's switch, as [`QrGuardrailFields::enabled`] takes it: optional, and written as
the switch when sent.

PublishReasonCodesRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/reason-codes` body: the `(tenant, store)` to push the tenant's authored list
to. Like every other node publish, the entries come from what is authored, not from the body.

PublishRetentionRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/retention` body: how many days a store's edge keeps a synced event
(ADR-0145).

PublishRolloutRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/ota` body: the `(tenant, store)` and the rollout to publish. There is no
`halted` field — a fresh publish is live; the kill switch is `POST /admin/config/ota/halt`.

PublishStoreProfileRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/config/store-profile` body: the `(tenant, store)` and who that store legally is.

Every field is text the operator supplies. A registered address is written differently in every
country, so the framework imposes no shape on it; the one field with a checkable shape is the tax
registration number, and the check is the **country module's**
([ADR-0106](../../../docs/adr/0106-the-store-is-a-legal-person.md)).

country_code.description:
Which country's rule to check the registration number's *shape* against, as an ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 code. Optional: a fork whose country module is not compiled into this cloud still
publishes a profile, with the number stored unchecked rather than the publish refused.

legal_name.description: The registered name — what the law wants on the paper.

PublishTaxRequest.description:
A super-admin publishes a tenant's authored tax rates to one of its stores: the `(tenant, store)`.
The rates come from the authored table, not the body — publishing is "push what is authored".

PublishTenderRequest.description: A `PUT /admin/config/tender` body: the `(tenant, store)` and the accepted payment-method tokens.

arguments.description:
That node's own arguments: the single-store body minus the `(tenant, store)`. Nodes
compiled from tenant-wide authoring (`tax`, `campaigns`, `inventory`, `reason_codes`,
`permissions`, `floor`) take none, and an object is accepted and ignored for them.

node.description: Which node kind to publish — one of the thirteen batchable ones (ADR-0122 §4).

PublishVendorsRequest.description: A `PUT /admin/config/vendors` body: the store and its per-marketplace policies.

oneOf.description: A percentage off the base.

rate.description: The rate, as an exact ratio (e.g. 10/100 for 10%).

oneOf.description: A fixed amount off the base, in the base's currency.

PublishedAction.description: What a campaign takes off. Wire mirror of `pos_core::campaign::Action`.

PublishedCampaign.description:
One authored campaign, in wire form. Faithful mirror of `pos_core::campaign::Campaign` plus the
authoring `name` the console and receipt show (the engine does not need a name to evaluate).

conditions.description: What must hold for it to apply.

exclusion_group.description:
An exclusion group: at most one campaign per group applies to a bill. Absent means it stacks
with everything.

id.description: Its stable id — the tiebreak that makes evaluation order total.

kind.description: Which of the five kinds it is.

name.description:
The operator-facing name, shown on the receipt line, the audit trail, and the console. Not
used by evaluation.

priority.description: Priority within its kind and exclusion group; higher applies first.

quota_remaining.description: Remaining quota; absent is unlimited, `Some(0)` is exhausted.

PublishedCampaignKind.description:
The five campaign kinds, in the order the pricing spec (§7) evaluates them. Wire mirror of
`pos_core::campaign::CampaignKind`.

PublishedChannels.description: The `channels` config node: the sales channels a store accepts orders on.

enabled.description:
The enabled channels. An empty list published means the store accepts no channel; an *absent*
node (never published) means no restriction — see the module docs.

PublishedConditions.description:
The conditions a campaign requires before it applies. Wire mirror of
`pos_core::campaign::Conditions`; every field is optional and absent means unrestricted.

channels.description:
The sales channels it applies on. Absent means every channel. Wrapped in [`Open`] so a
channel token from a newer cloud round-trips rather than failing the whole node.

oneOf.description: A minimum bill total. Absent means no minimum.
The weekly schedule window. Absent means always active.

PublishedConfig.description: The version id a successful publish produced.

config_version_id.description: The new config version id (a ULID).

PublishedFee.description:
One fee rule: what it is called, what it charges, on which channels and items, and how it is
taxed.

No `deny_unknown_fields`, as for every published node: an edge on an older release applies a
rule that carries a field it does not know, rather than refusing the whole node. Read the enum
fields through [`kind`](Self::kind()), [`item_scope`](Self::item_scope()) and
[`tax`](Self::tax()), which give an absent value its default and refuse an unknown one where a
guess would be a price. [`violations`](Self::violations) is the shape check ADR-0159 has the
cloud make before it publishes a rule.

active.description:
Whether the rule applies at all. Absent means `true`: a rule the cloud publishes applies
unless it is paused.

oneOf.description:
For [`FeeKind::AmountPerBill`] and [`FeeKind::AmountPerUnit`]: the charge, an integer in the
currency's minor unit. Ignored for a percentage.

base_discounted.description:
For a percentage: whether the base is discounted, that is taken after discounts and comps
(`true`), or before them (`false`). Absent means `true`, as the owner confirmed.

base_tax_inclusive.description:
For a percentage: whether the base is tax-inclusive (`true`), for a market that quotes a
charge on the tax-inclusive price, or net of tax (`false`). Absent means `false`, as the
owner confirmed.

channels.description:
The sales channels the fee applies on. Empty, which is what an absent field reads as, means
every channel. Each is wrapped in [`Open`] so a channel from a newer cloud round-trips; one
this build does not recognise matches no channel. Read through
[`applies_on`](Self::applies_on).

code.description: The short handle a report groups by.

display_name.description:
The name the bill prints the fee under. Always present, and the fallback for any locale
[`display_name_translations`](Self::display_name_translations) does not carry
(`docs/pos-spec.md` §12: English is always present and is the fallback).

display_name_translations.description:
The name in each locale it is translated into, keyed by locale code (`"vi"`, `"ja"`, …), as
[`crate::reason_codes::PublishedReasonCode::display_name_translations`] does for a reason.
Read through [`localized_name`](Self::localized_name).

fee_id.description:
Its stable id: the same fee across a rename, and the key ADR-0159 merges a tenant's, a
brand's and a store's rules by.

item_scope.description:
Which lines the fee counts, together with [`menu_item_ids`](Self::menu_item_ids). Read
through [`item_scope`](Self::item_scope()) and [`counts_item`](Self::counts_item); absent
means every line.

kind.description:
How the fee is charged. Read it through [`kind`](Self::kind()): an absent or unknown kind is
no kind, and a rule of no kind applies to nothing. Absent parses, so one such rule does not
stop a store applying the rest of the node.

menu_item_ids.description:
The items a [`FeeItems::Include`] or [`FeeItems::Exclude`] scope lists, by id rather than by
category (the module documentation says why). Ignored for [`FeeItems::All`].

oneOf.description:
For [`FeeKind::Percent`]: the share of the base, as an exact ratio. 5 % is
`Ratio::percent(5)` and 2.5 % is `Ratio::basis_points(250)`; never a float. Ignored for the
amount kinds.

tax.description:
How the fee is taxed. Read it through [`tax`](Self::tax()), which reads an absent or unknown
treatment as [`FeeTax::FollowLines`].

oneOf.description: For [`FeeTax::TaxClass`]: the class the fee is taxed at. Ignored otherwise.

waivable.description:
Whether staff may take the fee off one bill. Absent means `false`, as the owner confirmed.
Waiving is an act on a bill, under its own permission and with a reason
(ADR-0159 decision 5), never an edit of this rule.

PublishedIngredient.description: One ingredient held in stock, in wire form: its id, a display name, and the unit it is counted in.

id.description: Its stable id.

name.description: The operator-facing name, shown in the console and the recipe editor.

unit.description:
The unit it is stocked and consumed in. Wrapped in [`Open`] so a unit token from a newer cloud
round-trips rather than failing the whole node.

PublishedMenu.description: What a menu publish answers: the version it produced, and how the store's fees went with it.

config_version_id.description: The new config version id (a ULID).

fees.description:
The store's `fees` node, composed on the tree the menu was written onto, with a fee
publish's outcomes: applied in the same version, unchanged, refused with each rule the store
cannot apply and why, or failed. Only an applied one wrote anything.

PublishedOrigins.description:
The `origins` config node: the origins a store's edge answers beside the one that served the
request.

The serving origin is never in this list and never needs to be — the edge compares it against the
request's own `Host`, so a store that has published nothing keeps serving its own UI.

PublishedQr.description:
The `qr` node: its setting, and the guardrails the console's QR form writes beside it.

Each guardrail is `None` where the node does not carry it, or carries something other than its
JSON type, and each is left off the wire while absent.

oneOf.description:
The hours the store takes QR orders. Absent, or without a whole open and close hour, is
always open.

enabled.description:
QR ordering's switch as the node carries it. The switch itself is the store's
`qr_ordering_enabled` flag (ADR-0160 decision 5), and a cloud that knows it writes this equal
to it, so a `false` flag beside a value that is not `false` is the flag from before the
switch.

per_table_limit.description:
How many guest orders one table may submit within the rate window. Absent is the guest
intake's default.

rate_window_secs.description: The rate window, in seconds. Absent is the guest intake's default.

staff_confirmation_required.description:
Whether a table-bearing guest order waits for a member of staff before the kitchen sees it.
Absent is `true` to both readers (ADR-0057): a store that never said holds guest orders.

table_order.description:
What a guest's order does at a table that already has an open order. Read it through
[`PublishedQr::table_order`], which gives an absent or unknown value its default.

PublishedReasonCode.description: One entry in the managed list: what it is called, and what it may be given for.

active.description:
Whether staff may still pick it. An inactive entry stays in the list so historic events
keep resolving, and disappears from every picker. Absent in the document means active.

applies_to.description:
The actions this reason may be given for.

Empty means the entry is valid for nothing, which is a data-entry mistake rather than a
posture — the publish refuses it (ADR-0115), because an unusable row in a picker is worse
than a missing one. Each action is wrapped in [`Open`] so an action token from a newer
cloud round-trips instead of failing the whole node; an unrecognised one matches nothing,
which is the conservative answer for a fraud control.

code.description: The short handle a report groups by.

display_name.description:
The name staff read on the picker. Always present, and the fallback for any locale
[`display_name_translations`](Self::display_name_translations) does not carry (§12: English
is always present and is the fallback).

display_name_translations.description:
The name in each locale it is translated into, keyed by locale code (`"vi"`, `"ja"`, …), as
[`crate::menu::MenuEntry::display_name_translations`] does for an item. Additive: an entry
with none behaves exactly as one that predates the field.

id.description: Its stable id — the value an event's `reason_code_id` carries.

PublishedRecipe.description:
The bill of materials for one makeable thing — a menu item or a modifier — plus its auto-86
threshold. A modifier carries its own [`MenuItemId`] and its own recipe (the "large" size adds its
extra dough), so it is a recipe like any other.

auto_86_threshold.description:
The auto-86 threshold (§8): the item is sold while strictly more than this many can be made,
and marked unavailable at or below it. Defaults to `0` — 86 only when nothing can be made.

item.description: The item or modifier this recipe makes.

lines.description:
The ingredients and per-unit amounts. Empty means the item consumes nothing tracked and is
never limited by stock.

PublishedRecipeLine.description:
One line of a recipe: an ingredient and how much of it one unit of the item (or modifier) consumes,
in that ingredient's own unit. Wire mirror of `pos_core::inventory::RecipeLine`.

per_unit.description: How much of it one unit of the item consumes (a [`Quantity`] in thousandths of the unit).

PublishedRetention.description:
The `retention` node.

No `deny_unknown_fields`, as for every published node: an edge on an older release applies a node
that carries a field it does not know, rather than refusing the whole document.

event_log_days.description:
How many days the edge keeps a synced event, as the node carries it: a whole number, and
`None` for anything else. Read it through [`PublishedRetention::event_log_days`].

PublishedSchedule.description:
A weekly schedule window. Wire mirror of `pos_core::campaign::Schedule`; the window is half-open
and may wrap past midnight (`start_minute > end_minute`).

days.description:
The weekday bitmask, `Monday` = bit 0 — the same 7-bit mask
`pos_core::campaign::WeekdaySet` uses (bits above Sunday are ignored).

end_minute.description: The first excluded minute of the day, 0–1439.

start_minute.description: The first included minute of the day, 0–1439.

PublishedSupplier.description:
A supplier a store receives goods from — a lightweight reference only (id + name). The full
purchasing relationship lives in the ERP (§19).

id.description: Its stable id.

PublishedTender.description: The `tender` config node: the payment methods a store accepts.

accepted.description:
The accepted payment methods. An empty list published means the store takes no tender; an
*absent* node means no restriction — any known method is accepted, as before M7.

PublishedVendorPolicies.description: The `vendors` config node: a store's per-marketplace policies.

PublishedVendorPolicy.description:
One store's policy toward a single delivery marketplace, in wire form ([ADR-0080](../../../docs/adr/0080-channels-and-payments.md), M7).

A lightweight authoring shape only: which vendor, whether it is on, its availability (open/busy/
closed, mirroring the `DeliveryVendor` busy-mode), the prep time authored for the busy case, and the
menu items suppressed (86'd) on that vendor. The live loop that pushes this to a marketplace is the
flagged follow-up; publishing the policy is this track.

availability.description: The store's availability to this vendor. Wrapped in [`Open`] for forward-compatibility.

enabled.description: Whether the store currently offers orders to this vendor at all.

prep_minutes.description:
The prep time (minutes) authored for the busy case — how long the vendor should quote while the
store is throttling. `0` means "use the vendor's default".

suppressed_items.description: Menu items suppressed (86'd) on this vendor specifically, independent of stock-driven auto-86.

vendor.description: The vendor's operator-facing name (e.g. the marketplace brand). Reference/display only.

PutSettingRequest.description: A `PUT /admin/settings` body: one value, at one scope.

notice_confirmed.description: Whether the person confirmed the notice of a value that needs it (ADR-0169 decision 2).

scope_id.description: The tenant, brand, store group or store the value is for.

QrBusinessHours.description:
The hours a store takes QR orders, as the `qr` node carries them.

Read only through the node ([`PublishedQr`]), field by field: an open or close hour that is not a
whole number from 0 to 255 leaves the store with no hours, which is always open, and an offset
that is not a whole number reads as absent. The guest intake reads an hour past 23 as no hours
too, as the console refuses to write one.

close_hour.description:
The hour orders close. An open hour later than the close hour wraps past midnight, and one
equal to it is always open.

open_hour.description: The hour orders open, in the store's offset from UTC.

tz_offset_minutes.description: The store's offset from UTC, in minutes. Absent reads as UTC.

Quantity.description:
A quantity, counted in thousandths of a unit.

The wire form is the integer count of thousandths, so 1.5 is `1500`. Naming it
`milli` rather than `value` keeps the scale visible at every use site.

Ratio.description:
An exact rational rate: a tax rate, a service charge, a percentage discount.

A rate is never a float. 10% is `Ratio::percent(10)`, which is 10/100 exactly,
and 8.25% is `Ratio::basis_points(825)`.

On the wire it is two integers, `{"numerator": 10, "denominator": 100}`. It has to
cross a boundary because a line snapshot captures **the tax rate in force at the
moment the line was added** (`docs/pos-spec.md` §14.2) — sending a decimal string
or a float instead would reintroduce exactly the imprecision the integer discipline
exists to prevent. `NonZeroI64` means a zero denominator is unrepresentable, so a
malformed rate is rejected at the edge rather than dividing by zero later.

ReasonCode.description:
A short, stable, language-independent handle for a reason — `"WASTE"`, `"STAFF_ERROR"`.

Deliberately not in [`crate::text`], which holds the text types admissible in an *event
payload*. This one is never in a payload: an event carries the [`ReasonCodeId`], and the code
exists so a report can group by something an operator recognises rather than by a ULID
(`docs/pos-spec.md` §11 item 3 compares void and discount rates per employee) and so a CSV
export is readable.

ReasonCodeId.description: A `ReasonCodeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ReasonCodeRequest.description:
A create/update body for a reason code. The id is **server-owned** — minted on create, the path
id on update — so a client never supplies or forges the value historic events cite forever.

`code`, `display_name`, `display_name_translations`, `applies_to` and `active` are the wire
entry's own fields, reused rather than re-declared, except that the two name fields arrive as
plain strings so a blank a form left behind can be trimmed away before it becomes a
[`DisplayName`].

active.description:
Whether staff may still pick it. Absent means active, matching the wire node's own default —
a caller that omits it is authoring a usable reason, not a retired one.

display_name_translations.description:
Per-locale names keyed by locale code (`docs/pos-spec.md` §12). Optional and additive;
`display_name` is the always-present fallback.

ReasonCodesPublished.description: What a reason-code publish answers: the version it made, and what the store now holds.

active.description: How many of them are active.

config_version_id.description: The new config version, a ULID.

published.description: How many reason codes were published.

uncovered_actions.description: The actions no active reason code covers, which nobody can now record.

RecipeRequest.description:
The body of a recipe write. The item it makes is the URL key on the `PUT` — a recipe references
an existing menu item or modifier, so its id is client-owned, unlike an ingredient's
server-minted id. `lines` (the bill of materials) and `auto_86_threshold` are the wire recipe's
own fields.

ReconcileRunView.description:
One reconciliation run on the wire ([ADR-0078](../../../docs/adr/0078-sync-and-ota-closure.md)):
counts and a timestamp, never event contents or a customer identifier.

candidates_offered.description: How many ids the edge offered in its manifest.

missing_found.description: How many of them the cloud was missing (asked the edge to re-push); zero means fully in sync.

run_id.description: The run's id (a ULID string; chronological).

store_id.description: The store the diff was for (a ULID string).

RecoveryCodesResponse.description:
The freshly-generated recovery codes, returned exactly once. [`fmt::Debug`] redacts the codes so
they cannot reach a log — they exist in the response body and nowhere else.

codes.description: The plaintext codes, shown this once; only their hashes are stored.

remaining.description: How many codes are now available (the count just generated).

RecoveryCodesStatus.description: How many unused recovery codes the acting admin has left — the codes themselves are never listed.

remaining.description: The number of unused recovery codes.

ReenrolTotpRequest.description:
A request to re-enrol TOTP: the current password, re-confirming the knowledge factor before the
possession factor is rotated. [`fmt::Debug`] redacts it.

RegionAcknowledgementView.description:
A recorded answer to a store's region difference, as the console sees it
([ADR-0114](../../../docs/adr/0114-region-is-required-recorded-visible.md)).

The two country codes ride along rather than being left implicit: the console renders them in
the sentence it shows ("data in SG, store registered in VN — acknowledged"), and a reader of the
payload can see *what* was answered without inferring it from the fields beside it.

No `acknowledged_by`. The row does not carry one — the audit action
`store.edge_placement.acknowledge` does, and it is the copy that survives the next answer. The
console links to the store's audit tab rather than showing a name this read cannot honestly give.

acknowledged_at_ms.description:
When it was written, in milliseconds since the epoch — the same representation every other
instant on this read uses.

profile_country.description: The country the store was registered in when the answer was written.

reason.description: Why the difference is correct, as somebody typed it. Carried verbatim, never parsed.

region_country.description: The country its data was resting in when the answer was written.

RegisterWebhookRequest.description: A super-admin request to register a webhook endpoint for a tenant.

store_id.description: The store whose event log the endpoint follows (a 26-character ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant the endpoint belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

url.description:
The destination URL. Must be `https`, must carry no credentials, and must resolve only to
public-unicast addresses — vetted here before the endpoint is stored ([ADR-0032](../../../docs/adr/0032-webhooks.md)).

RegisterWebhookResponse.description:
The one-time response to a registration: the id, the normalized URL, and the signing secret shown
**exactly once** — the tenant needs it to verify the HMAC signature on every delivery, and the
cloud keeps only its own copy thereafter.

id.description: The endpoint's public id (a ULID).

signing_secret.description: The HMAC signing secret. Shown once; it is the tenant's copy of what the cloud signs with.

url.description: The normalized destination URL that was stored.

ReleaseArtifacts.description: What a release's artifact list answers: the release and each artifact it hosts.

ReleaseFetched.description: What a release fetch answers: the release, the forge's tag for it, and each artifact it hosted.

artifacts.description: Each artifact the fetch put in the cloud.

release.description: The release, as the console named it.

tag.description: The tag the forge published it under.

ReleaseList.description: What the release list answers: the tenant's releases, newest first.

releases.description: Each release, as its own read reports it.

ReleaseNodeRequest.description: One node of a release, and the arguments its plan needs — the same pair a batch publish takes.

ReleasePairView.description:
One `(node, store)` cell of the report — F9's whole point.

`failure` is why the pair last could not apply. A pair that failed is still `PENDING`: the
activator retries it, and what an operator needs meanwhile is the reason, not a status that
pretends the attempt never happened.

resolved_timezone.description:
The IANA zone `effective_at_ms` was resolved against, or `None`.

What turns the instant back into the sentence the operator approved. A wall-clock release is
one instant per timezone (ADR-0125 §2), and a console that prints the instant without the
clock it came from draws every shop's 04:00 in the reader's own time — which is the review
ADR-0125 §26 rejected fire-time conversion to avoid. `None` for a release timed as a plain
UTC instant, which has no per-store clock, and for pairs written before the column existed.

status.description: The same spelling `GET /admin/config/scheduled` already gives this exact row.

ReleaseReport.description: A release and the grid of its pairs.

ReleaseStatus.description:
Where a release stands. Derived from its pairs, stored so a list read need not aggregate.

`Partial` is the state the whole record exists for: N × M writes fail individually, and at forty
stores an operator needs the two shops that did not take it, not a red cross over the fleet. There
is no `RolledBack` — an applied write is a config version, and the way back is
[ADR-0095](../../../docs/adr/0095-conditional-writes-for-collections.md)'s version history.

ReleaseTenantRequest.description: A body carrying nothing but the tenant — what `cancel` needs, since the id is in the path.

instant_at_ms.description: The single instant, for a release timed in UTC. Null for a wall-clock release.

status.description:
Serialised as the enum, not as `as_wire()`: `as_wire` is the **stored** token (`SCHEDULED`),
and every other status on this surface reaches the console `snake_case`. Two spellings for one
concept is two branches in the console's type for no gain.

wall_clock_date.description: The operator's local date, for a wall-clock release. Null for an instant release.

RetireHandoverRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/lease/retire` body: which store's settled handover is being retired.

No generation, and that asymmetry with settle is deliberate. Settle is an attestation about one
named machine's disk; retire is a decision about the handover the row currently describes, and
the row's own preconditions — settled, and not already retired — are what make it unambiguous.

RevokeActivationRequest.description: A super-admin cancels the pending activation for a device slot (a leaked setup sheet).

device_id.description: The device slot whose issued codes to cancel (a ULID).

store_id.description: The store the device belongs to (a ULID).

tenant_id.description: The tenant the device belongs to (a ULID).

RevokeActivationResponse.description: How many still-issued codes were cancelled.

revoked.description: The number of codes moved from `issued` to `revoked`.

RevokeDeviceRequest.description:
Retire one till on a store: the tenant it belongs to and the store-minted local device id.

`local_device_id` is the id from `GET /admin/stores/{id}/devices/admitted` — the store's own,
**not** a console `Device.device_id`. Nothing joins those two identity spaces, so an id taken
from the wrong list names a device the store has never had, and the store records it as done
without retiring anything.

RoleReadiness.description: One active role held at the store, and what it does not grant.

missing.description: What it does not grant, everyday permissions first.

name.description: The role's name — a job, never a person's.

people.description:
How many people on the store's roster hold it, each counted once however many of their
assignments name it.

RoleTemplate.description:
A tenant's named role — a stored subset of the `pos-core` permission catalogue (§9). One tenant's
*Manager* is not another's, so templates are per-tenant. Archived, never deleted, so an assignment
or published permission set that references it stays reconcilable.

discount_ceiling_minor.description:
How much this role may discount before it needs a manager, in the currency's minor unit.

`billing.discount.apply` is granted to a **server** and is not PIN-flagged; its own
description is *"apply a discount up to the role's configured ceiling"*, and until this field
existed there was nowhere to configure one. The edge reads an absent ceiling as **zero**
rather than as "no limit" — the safe direction — so a role that leaves this `None` keeps
today's behaviour exactly: every discount needs `billing.discount.override_ceiling` and a
manager's PIN.

`None` and `Some(0)` land in the same place and are not the same statement. The first is an
absence; the second is a tenant saying this role discounts nothing. Never negative — the
column refuses it, and so does the route.

name.description: The human role name (e.g. *Cashier*), unique within the tenant.

permissions.description:
The permission ids the role grants **directly**, each a `pos-core` catalogue id: its holder
acts on them alone.

permissions_with_approval.description:
The permission ids the role grants only **with approval**: another person who holds one
directly enters their code and PIN for each act
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 4). Each is a PIN-flagged catalogue id, and none is also in [`Self::permissions`].
Always on the wire, empty for a role that grants everything directly.

RoleTemplateId.description: A role template's identifier — a ULID minted at creation.

RollbackConfigRequest.description: A super-admin rolls a store's config back to a past version.

version_id.description: The version to restore (a ULID); its effective document becomes the new current version.

RoutingRuleId.description:
A routing rule's identifier — a ULID minted at creation. Cloud-local (like `pos-cloud`'s
`people::EmployeeId`): a rule is authoring-only and compiles into the
`stations` node's flat routing list, which carries no rule id.

oneOf.description: The key is new — the import would add it.
The key exists — the import would overwrite its row.
The row is invalid and would be skipped; `reason` says why.

reason.description: A human-readable reason the row was rejected (e.g. `missing en value`).

RowAction.description:
What an import would do to one row. Serialises with an `action` tag and, for a rejection, a
`reason` — the shape the dashboard renders row-by-row.

SampleBillView.description:
A sample bill as the console draws it: each line, each fee with its tax, the tax per class, and
what the guest would pay.

service_charge.description: Every fee together, as the bill's one service-charge figure carries it.

SampleFeeLineView.description: A fee the sample bill charges, with its tax.

class_shares.description: The parts of the fee taxed at each class, with each part's tax.

SampleFeeShareView.description: The part of a fee taxed at one class.

SampleLineRequest.description: One sample line: an item on the store's menu, and how many.

SampleLineView.description: A sample line, priced from the store's menu.

SampleTaxLineView.description: The tax at one class, on the base the fees joined.

ScheduleCampaignsRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/campaigns/schedule` body: the `(tenant, store)` and the future instant the
snapshot should publish, Unix milliseconds.

nodes.description: The nodes to carry, in any order — the activator applies them in dependency order per store.

store_ids.description: The stores, explicitly. Omitted, the release's `target_group_id` is expanded instead.

ScheduledPublishView.description:
A scheduled publish as listed — metadata only; the snapshotted node value is not returned (it can
be large, and the console shows what and when, not the payload).

ScopeLevel.description:
Which layer of the config tree a connection serves.

The tree's own layers ([ADR-0033](../../../docs/adr/0033-config-tree.md)), so a connection is
inherited the way every other setting is: a store uses its own, or its brand's, or the tenant's.

SetDrawerRequest.description: An operator marks an approved printer as having a cash drawer wired to it, or clears the mark.

drawer_attached.description: Whether a cash drawer is on this printer's kick port.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the device belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

SetFloatRequest.description:
An operator says what an approved terminal's drawer opens with by default.

The float is the till's whole float state, as the receipt fields are its receipt state: an absent
or `null` float is the store's again.

opening_float_minor.description:
The float, a whole amount in the store currency's minor unit, or `null` for the store's
`shift.opening_float_minor`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the terminal belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

SetPaperRequest.description: An operator says what paper an approved printer takes and whether it cuts it.

cuts_paper.description: Whether the printer cuts its paper: `false` for one with no cutter.

paper_width.description: The paper the printer takes, as its `PAPER_WIDTH_…` token.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the device belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

SetPinRequest.description:
Set or reset an employee's sign-in PIN. The digits are hashed here and never stored or logged in
the clear (ADR-0070); the request body is the only place they appear, and it is never audited.

SetPrintAgentRequest.description: An operator points an approved device at the terminal that holds its transport, or clears it.

agent_device_id.description:
The terminal whose agent will write this printer's bytes (a ULID), or `null` to go back to
the edge opening the address itself.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the device belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

SetReceiptRequest.description:
An operator says where an approved terminal's receipts go and the languages they print in.

The three fields are the till's whole receipt state, as a station's update is its whole state: an
absent or `null` field is the store's again.

receipt_language.description: The language they print in, as a `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_…` token, or `null` for the store's.

receipt_printer_id.description:
The printer this till's receipts, receipt copies and pre-bills go to (a ULID), or `null` for
the store's receipt printer.

receipt_second_language.description:
The second language they print in, as a `RECEIPT_SECOND_LANGUAGE_…` token, or `null` for the
store's.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the terminal belongs to (a 26-character ULID).

SetStoreGroupMembersRequest.description:
A `PUT /admin/store-groups/{group_id}/members` body: the whole membership, not a delta.

Wholesale rather than add/remove because the operator's mental model is a *set* — "these are the
airport shops" — and a delta API makes two admins' concurrent edits merge into a cohort neither
of them chose. Under `If-Match` (ADR-0095 shape C) the second one is refused instead.

SetTaxRatesRequest.description: A `PUT /admin/catalog/tax-rates` body: the tenant and its whole rate table (a wholesale replace).

SettingCatalogueEntry.description:
One setting as the console's settings screen draws it: the register entry, without its
summary. The screen labels a setting and each of its values from its own translations, keyed by
the setting's key, so no English sentence reaches it from here.

What else it carries depends on the kind: a choice's `values`; a whole number's `min`, `max` and
`unit`, which the screen bounds its input by and names in the operator's language; nothing more
for a switch. `default` and `preset` are the value as the node carries it — a token, a number or
a boolean. `confirm` is a value written only with a recorded confirmation (ADR-0169).

SettingPublishOutcome.description: How one store's settings publish went, as its token.

SettingPublishResult.description: How one store's settings publish went.

oneOf.description: A `CHOICE`'s token
An `INT`'s whole number
A `BOOL`

SettingValueSchema.description: A setting's value, in the shape its kind gives it

SettingValues.description: What the settings list answers: every value the tenant has written, at every scope.

SettingsCatalogue.description: What the settings catalogue answers: every setting the register declares.

settings.description: One entry per setting, in register order.

SettingsStoreRequest.description: A store to publish settings to, or every store of the tenant.

SettleHandoverRequest.description:
A `POST /admin/config/lease/settle` body: the store, and the generation the caller is attesting
has nothing left on it.

`superseded_generation` is required and is the whole precondition. It is not "which handover do
you mean" — one store has at most one in flight — it is the caller stating *which machine* they
checked. A settle that took no number would let a stale console close a handover the operator
never looked at.

SetupRequest.description:
A first-boot enrolment request: the authorising setup token and the password the operator chooses.

[`fmt::Debug`] redacts both, so a logged request cannot leak the token or the password.

password.description: The password the operator is choosing for the super-admin.

setup_token.description: The one-time setup token (`bootstrap.sh` minted it into `cloud.toml`).

Station.description:
A kitchen station as the console reads it: a station on one store's line, with an optional backup
(the printer failover) and a catch-all `is_default` flag.

oneOf.description: The failover target when this station's printer is down, or `None` for no backup.

is_default.description: Whether this is the store's catch-all station (a fired line with no matching rule).

late_after_seconds.description:
How long a ticket at this station waits, in seconds, before the kitchen display marks it
late, or `None` for the default the edge reads (ADR-0160 decision 2).

store_id.description: The store this station belongs to.

ticket_language.description:
The language its kitchen tickets print in, as the `RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_…` token it was saved
with, or `None` for the store's display language (ADR-0160 decision 2). Kept as the token so
the publish carries it as stored.

StationId.description: A `StationId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

StoreArchivesResponse.description: The answer: what this store has, newest first.

StoreFault.description:
Why a store cannot apply a rule it would be sent. Each one would fail every bill the rule
applies to, so a store with one is not sent its rules at all.

StoreGroup.description: A cohort of stores an operator publishes to as one.

status.description:
Active or archived. An archived group keeps its membership (so the record of what it *was*
survives) and is refused as a batch target.

StoreGroupId.description:
A store group's identifier — a ULID minted when the group is created.

Like `pos-cloud-catalog`'s `MenuId` it never crosses the store wire: a group is an authoring
and delivery concept in the cloud, and what reaches a store is the same config node it would have
received from a single publish.

StoreGroupMembership.description:
What a membership write answers: the members as stored, the group's new version, and how the
`permissions` publish went at each store whose staff it moved.

etag.description: The group's new version, as the `ETag` header carries it.

store_ids.description: The member stores, each a ULID, in the order first named.

stores.description: One result per store whose staff the change moved.

StoreGroupView.description:
A store group on the wire, with its membership.

Members ride along with the list rather than needing a read per group: the console's first
question about a cohort is how big it is, and a screen that had to fetch each one would show a
list of names with the counts arriving afterwards.

StoreId.description: A `StoreId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

StoreRecord.description:
A store — grouped under a tenant and, optionally, a brand. Shares its `store_id` with its
`config_trees` row.

oneOf.description: The owning brand, or `None` until an operator assigns one.

name.description: The human name (a placeholder until renamed).

store_id.description: The store id.

StoredSettingValue.description: One value written at one scope.

scope.description: The scope the value was written at.

scope_id.description: The tenant, brand, store group or store it was written for.

update_time.description: When it was written. Decides between two store groups that disagree.

value.description: The value, as the node carries it.

StoresPublished_FeePublishResult.description:
What a write that publishes to several stores at once answers: one result per store it reached,
in the order it reached them.

items.description: How one store's fee publish went.

faults.description: For a refused store: each rule it cannot apply, and why.

StoresPublished_PermissionsPublishResult.description:
What a write that publishes to several stores at once answers: one result per store it reached,
in the order it reached them.

items.description: How one store's `permissions` publish went, as a write that publishes at once reports it.

StoresPublished_SettingPublishResult.description:
What a write that publishes to several stores at once answers: one result per store it reached,
in the order it reached them.

items.description: How one store's settings publish went.

SubjectErased.description: What an erasure answers: that it is done, and whether the record was already masked.

already_masked.description: Whether it was masked before this request.

erased.description: Always `true`: the record is masked now.

SubjectExportView.description:
A subject export — the portability/access payload: the record with its field values. This is the one
route that returns the personal data, and only to an operator holding `console.subjects.manage`; the
audit trail records that an export happened and how many fields, never the values.

SubjectMetaView.description:
A subject lookup — existence and status, without the personal fields. What a lookup returns so the
operator can confirm the right subject before exporting or erasing; the values only leave the server
on an explicit export.

field_count.description: How many personal fields the record has, so the operator sees there is data without seeing it.

masked.description: Whether the personal data has already been masked (erased) — a masked row holds no PII.

SupplierId.description: A `SupplierId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

SupplierRequest.description: A create/update body for a supplier. The id is **server-owned**, exactly like an ingredient's.

Table.description:
A table as the console reads it: a table on one store's floor, in an area, optionally placed on the
editor's grid.

oneOf.description: Where it sits in the floor editor's grid, or `None` if not yet placed.

seats.description: How many covers it seats (zero means unspecified).

store_id.description: The store this table belongs to.

TableId.description: A `TableId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

TableQrEntry.description:
One table's printable QR: its id, the label a host reads, and the signed token the guest's QR
carries. The token binds `(tenant, store, table)` — no personal data — and is the same value
`verify_table_token` checks on a guest order (ADR-0057).

TableQrView.description: The store's table QR tokens, for the console's printable sheet.

TaskHealthReport.description:
The whole-fleet-of-loops report: an overall verdict (every *expected* loop is healthy) plus the
per-loop views. Extra loops that ticked but the deployment does not expect are reported too
(`expected: false`), so nothing is hidden, but they do not sway the overall verdict.

TaskHealthView.description:
One background loop as the console sees it: identity, whether the deployment expects it to run, a
health verdict derived at read time, when it last ticked, and its self-describing detail.

TaxClass.description:
A tax class — a named bucket an item belongs to, whose rate the store's channel-keyed
[`pos_proto::locale::TaxRateTable`] resolves at reprice time (ADR-0066 entity 10; D6).

The class itself is country-agnostic (`alcohol`, `standard`, `takeaway-reduced`); the *rate* for
each `(tax_class, channel)` lives in the store's locale pack, not here. This entity exists so the
operator picks a tax class **by name** when authoring an item, instead of pasting a
[`TaxClassId`] ULID — the same "kill the ULID" move [ADR-0065](../../../docs/adr/0065-cloud-org-registry.md)
made for tenants and stores. Its id is the [`TaxClassId`] an item's `tax_class_id` references.

tax_class_id.description: The tax-class id — the [`TaxClassId`] an item references and the rate table is keyed by.

TaxClassId.description: A `TaxClassId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

TaxComponentTotal.description: One tax component's tax on a trading day, at one rate (part of [`DailyRevenue`]).

component_name.description:
The component's name as the bills recorded it, such as `CGST`: a
[`TaxComponentName`](pos_proto::locale::TaxComponentName) when it was folded. Text here, so
a stored day loads whatever a later release lets a name be.

rate_basis_points.description: Its part of the rate, in basis points: CGST at 2.5 % and at 9 % are two entries.

tax.description: Sum of the tax the day's tax lines recorded under it, minor units.

TaxComponentView.description: One named part of a rate, on the wire.

rate_bps.description: This part's share, in basis points.

components.description:
How the rate is broken out on the invoice. `#[serde(default)]`, so a console that predates
ADR-0104 still saves a grid and every row keeps printing as one line.

TaxRateView.description:
One authored tax-rate row on the wire: the class id, the channel's wire token, the rate in basis
points (10% is `1000`), and how that rate is broken out on the invoice.

component_name_invalid.description:
`true` when one of `components` is named with anything but a [`TaxComponentName`]: two to
eight upper-case letters and digits, starting with a letter
([ADR-0168](../../../docs/adr/0168-a-settled-bill-records-its-tax-components.md) decision 2).

Only a row saved before the grid checked names can be so. It is kept as it was saved, and
its stores charge its rate without a breakdown. A save replaces the whole grid and refuses
such a name, so the next save is refused until it is changed, which is what the console
flags. Absent otherwise, so a sound table reads as it always did. Output only: a save
reads no such field.

components.description:
The named parts the invoice prints, which must sum to `rate_bps`
([ADR-0104](../../../docs/adr/0104-multi-component-and-inclusive-tax.md)). Empty for a rate
printed as one line, which is most of the world.

TenantRecord.description: A tenant — the root of the tree.

Timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, as RFC 3339

TranslationGrid.description: A tenant's translation grid: content key → (locale → rendered string).

permissions_with_approval.description:

Update a station's name, backup, default flag, late threshold, ticket language, and status. Every

UpdateTableRequest.description: Update a table's area, label, seats, position, and status.

UploadedMedia.description: The `POST /admin/media` response: the id the caller references the new asset by, and its size.

Minted by the adapter, echoed by the client, compared only for equality.

allOf.description: An area as the console reads it: a named region of one store's floor.

store_id.description: The store this area belongs to.

etag.description:
The version [`record`](Self::record) was read at. Byte-identical to the `ETag` header
a single-resource read would carry, so a client never reformats it.

updated_at_ms.description:
When the row was last written, in Unix milliseconds — `None` where the adapter does not
project it.

Every one of these tables has carried an `updated_at` since it was created; not one read
ever returned it, so the console had no way to tell an operator whether what is on their
screen is newer than what the shop is running. The publish bar asked that question and had
to answer it from a within-session signal, which forgets on reload (Wave 4 · PR-5b, F13).

`Option` and skipped when absent, so this is additive twice over: the 80-odd existing
[`new`](Self::new) call sites compile untouched, and a read that does not project the
column serialises exactly the bytes it did before.

Versioned_Area.description:
A record together with the version it was read at.

Serialises as the record's own fields plus an `etag` — additive, so no existing field
moves or is renamed, and a list can carry a version per row where a header cannot.

Serialize only. This shape is something the cloud *writes*; the console reads it in TypeScript,
and no Rust caller parses one. Deriving `Deserialize` as well would pull in serde's flatten
buffer, whose `Content` enum carries `f32`/`f64` variants that `clippy.toml` bans outright —
a real cost (`docs/adr/0013`: money is never a float) for a capability nothing uses.

allOf.description:
An item in the catalog — the product master.

Its id is a [`MenuItemId`], the same identifier the compiled [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`] names and an
inbound order references: the item authored here is the item priced downstream. This slice carries
the fields a `MenuEntry` needs (name, tax class); its operational category, recipe/BOM link and
the rest arrive with later slices.

oneOf.description:
The course this item goes out on, or `None` for an item on no course
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md) decision 3).

Carried on the item exactly as [`tax_class_id`](Self::tax_class_id) is, and for the same
reason: a pizza is a main, and making a server say so on every tap would be a tap per dish
for a fact the catalog already knows. `None` is every item in every store today and stays
correct.

A **per-line override** is deliberately not modelled. The request it would serve — *"bring my
main with the starters"* — is about when the food goes, and firing already answers that;
relabelling a line's course to mean "sooner" would put a timing decision inside a taxonomy.

The item's photo — a [`MediaId`] into the media library (ADR-0075), or `None`. Authoring/display
only; it does not cross to the edge. A dangling ref (the asset was deleted) shows a placeholder.
The operational category this item reports under, or `None` if unclassified (entity 2).
The operational sub-category, refining the category, or `None` (entity 3).

menu_item_id.description: The item's id — shared with the compiled menu entry and any inbound order that names it.

name.description:
The human name (the default caption, before a layout overrides it per channel). Always
present, and the fallback for a locale [`name_translations`](Self::name_translations) omits.

name_translations.description:
The item's name in each locale it is translated into, keyed by locale code (`"vi"`, `"en"`, …)
([ADR-0074](../../../docs/adr/0074-localization-and-tax.md), Track M4). The compiler carries
these onto the [`pos_proto::MenuEntry`]; the store's display language selects one at the edge,
falling back to [`name`](Self::name). Additive — an item with none behaves as before.

allOf.description:
A course — the **service** taxonomy, when a dish goes out
([ADR-0130](../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md)).

Deliberately distinct from an [`ItemCategory`] (operational — what an item reports under) and from
a [`DisplayCategory`] (presentational — where a screen puts it). A dessert wine reports under
drinks and goes out with dessert, and collapsing any two of the three would make one of those
facts unsayable.

The `sort` is the point rather than decoration: "starter before main before dessert" is the
entire meaning of the grouping, and a set of names with no order is a taxonomy rather than a
service sequence. Ties break by id in the compiler, as everywhere else, so a re-compile of
unchanged authoring stays byte-identical.

Its id is [`pos_proto::ids::CourseId`], which has crossed the seam since the schema was written —
it is on `sales.order_line.added` and on a published routing rule. The entity is what was
missing.

sort.description:
Where it falls in the service sequence, ascending. Not unique: two courses a store considers
interchangeable may share a position, and forcing an operator to renumber the whole menu to
insert one between two others would be a worse rule than letting the id break the tie.

allOf.description:
A tenant's named role — a stored subset of the `pos-core` permission catalogue (§9). One tenant's
*Manager* is not another's, so templates are per-tenant. Archived, never deleted, so an assignment
or published permission set that references it stays reconcilable.

discount_ceiling_minor.description:
How much this role may discount before it needs a manager, in the currency's minor unit.

`billing.discount.apply` is granted to a **server** and is not PIN-flagged; its own
description is *"apply a discount up to the role's configured ceiling"*, and until this field
existed there was nowhere to configure one. The edge reads an absent ceiling as **zero**
rather than as "no limit" — the safe direction — so a role that leaves this `None` keeps
today's behaviour exactly: every discount needs `billing.discount.override_ceiling` and a
manager's PIN.

`None` and `Some(0)` land in the same place and are not the same statement. The first is an
absence; the second is a tenant saying this role discounts nothing. Never negative — the
column refuses it, and so does the route.

name.description: The human role name (e.g. *Cashier*), unique within the tenant.

permissions.description:
The permission ids the role grants **directly**, each a `pos-core` catalogue id: its holder
acts on them alone.

permissions_with_approval.description:
The permission ids the role grants only **with approval**: another person who holds one
directly enters their code and PIN for each act
([ADR-0158](../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 4). Each is a PIN-flagged catalogue id, and none is also in [`Self::permissions`].
Always on the wire, empty for a role that grants everything directly.

The version [`record`](Self::record) was read at. Byte-identical to the `ETag` header
a single-resource read would carry, so a client never reformats it.

updated_at_ms.description:
When the row was last written, in Unix milliseconds — `None` where the adapter does not
project it.

Every one of these tables has carried an `updated_at` since it was created; not one read
ever returned it, so the console had no way to tell an operator whether what is on their
screen is newer than what the shop is running. The publish bar asked that question and had
to answer it from a within-session signal, which forgets on reload (Wave 4 · PR-5b, F13).

`Option` and skipped when absent, so this is additive twice over: the 80-odd existing

ticket_language.description:

operator picks a tax class **by name** when authoring an item, instead of pasting a
[`TaxClassId`] ULID — the same "kill the ULID" move [ADR-0065](../../../docs/adr/0065-cloud-org-registry.md)
made for tenants and stores. Its id is the [`TaxClassId`] an item's `tax_class_id` references.

tax_class_id.description: The tax-class id — the [`TaxClassId`] an item references and the rate table is keyed by.
